name: Add click-triggered login picker
description: Turn the proven one-click Chrome slice into a usable multiple-account flow without widening browser permissions. Use focused DOM unit tests instead of a fixture site, then manually smoke-test the retained Autofill Demo item on the public demo page. name: Replace the error string slot with an actionable error object
description:
P0. appError is a single string (App.tsx:110); a second error overwrites the first, and inventory-truncation warnings share the slot with hard failures (App.tsx:174-176).

Raw backend strings currently reach the banner via errors.ts:1-7, e.g. 'fd0 bridge protocol mismatch: {n}' (bridge.ts:79), 'Untrusted IPC sender' (index.ts:612), 'fd0 window is unavailable' (13 sites), 'GitHub release lookup failed with HTTP {status}' (index.ts:247), 'Native agent supervision is unavailable in development mode' (agent-lifecycle.ts:85).

Separately, {ok:false} results are silently swallowed with zero feedback at App.tsx:511 (remove item), 931 (restore vault), 1837 (export recovery), ShareVaultModal.tsx:82 (remove member), 135 (import card) - user cancellation and backend refusal are indistinguishable.

Work:
- Model errors as {title, explanation, action?, detail?} instead of a string; stack rather than overwrite.
- Map known bridge/main failures to plain-language titles with a recovery action; keep the protocol text behind a 'Details' disclosure for support.
- Give every {ok:false} path an explicit outcome, distinguishing cancel from failure.

Do not change the bridge contract or error taxonomy on the Go side; map in the renderer.
result:
errors.ts now builds an AppError {title, detail, technical, severity, action} instead of a flat string, and the store keeps up to three at once rather than overwriting. Known bridge and main-process failures map to plain-language titles with a recovery action; the raw protocol text moves behind a 'Details' disclosure in the notice.

Every silently-swallowed {ok:false} path now produces an explicit outcome: remove item, remove member, import identity card, restore vault, export recovery, save attachment, and config import all say what happened instead of leaving the UI unchanged.

Toasts dedupe by text so a repeated action replaces its banner rather than stacking identical copies, and .toast-stack is pointer-events:none so a lingering toast can never intercept a click meant for the UI beneath it.

name: Plan platform local unlock support
description:
Design fd0 platform-local biometric/user-presence unlock end to end before implementation.

Goal:
Add a new fd0 auth method for local OS-protected unlock, covering macOS Touch ID/Secure Enclave or Keychain first and Linux/Framework Laptop via fprintd/PAM/Secret Service where possible. This must be a real auth method that unwraps fd0 K_unlock and super_priv through the existing user-chain/vault-wrap architecture, not a UI-only prompt in front of an already-available secret.

Core architecture requirement:
fd0-agent remains the single local unlock authority. CLI and future GUI both talk to the agent. The GUI may trigger native OS UI, but it must not become a second vault implementation and should not receive K_unlock, payload_key, or super_priv. If a platform needs foreground/UI process semantics, use an agent-owned helper or explicit security decision rather than silently moving secrets into the GUI.

Current architecture facts:
- User chain auth.set entries carry method_id, method_type, public_params, encrypted_super_priv.
- Vault wrapped_payload_keys carry method_id, method_type, public_params, wrap_nonce, wrapped.
- Existing method types are passphrase and yubikey.
- Passphrase derives K_unlock from Argon2id params.
- YubiKey stores a random K_unlock sealed to a hardware key and uses that K_unlock to decrypt encrypted_super_priv and vault payload_key.
- Server mostly stores signed opaque events; protocol-visible method_type/public_params changes affect clients, not server DB semantics.

Recommended protocol shape:
- Add method_type = platform-local, not fingerprint. Fingerprint is one possible local authentication policy; the useful primitive is a device-local OS protected secret released after user presence/biometric/system auth.
- public_params should be deterministic CBOR: PlatformLocalPublicParams { version, provider, key_ref, policy, flags }. Keep it minimal and non-secret.
- encrypted_super_priv remains unchanged: AEAD(K_unlock, super_priv, existing AAD).
- vault wrap remains unchanged: K_unlock wraps payload_key like other methods.

Provider model:
- macos-keychain-touchid: store/retrieve random 32-byte K_unlock in Keychain with LocalAuthentication access control requiring biometrics or device-owner auth.
- linux-secretservice-fprintd: verify user through fprintd/PAM, then retrieve random 32-byte K_unlock from Secret Service/KWallet/GNOME Keyring or a backend explicitly documented as local-user-session protected. This is weaker than Secure Enclave; document as OS-trust + biometric gate.
- Future providers can include windows-hello, tpm2, passkey/platform authenticator.

Non-goals for first implementation:
- Do not make biometric data part of cryptographic derivation. Fingerprints are not secrets and cannot be rotated.
- Do not support cross-device portability. This auth method is per-device; recovery/passphrase/YubiKey remains required.
- Do not allow platform-local as the only auth method unless recovery/export exists and UX explicitly confirms risk. Prefer requiring an existing unlocked session to enroll it.

Acceptance criteria for final implementation:
- docs/PROTOCOL.md updated with method_type, public_params CDDL, security semantics, client compatibility.
- internal/proto has PlatformLocalPublicParams and tests/golden compatibility.
- vault has PlatformLocalResolver with provider interface and strict validation.
- agent wire supports method_type platform-local without smuggling unrelated credentials.
- agent exposes a shared CLI/GUI-safe RPC/capability surface for platform-local unlock.
- CLI supports auth add --platform-local and unlock --method=platform-local with clear errors and fallback guidance.
- Future GUI can unlock through fd0-agent without handling raw K_unlock/super_priv.
- macOS provider has real Keychain/LocalAuthentication implementation or build-tagged stub with tests.
- Linux provider has fprintd/PAM preflight and a deliberate secret-backend decision before implementation.
- doctor reports platform-local method health: provider available, key_ref exists, policy readable where possible.
- tests cover unknown old clients failing clearly, bad public_params, missing key_ref, wrong provider, resolver returning bad K_unlock length, enrollment rollback atomicity.
- docs explain security: convenience unlock, device-local, OS trust boundary, never sole recovery.
result: Implemented platform-local auth end to end. Added method_type=platform-local and PlatformLocalPublicParams; vault resolver; agent unlock routing with no credential payload; CLI auth add/unlock UX; doctor structural checks; provider dispatcher; dev-local isolated test provider; macOS provider using LocalAuthentication user presence before device-local Keychain lookup; Linux provider using fprintd-verify plus Secret Service via secret-tool; best-effort provider cleanup on auth rm; protocol/threat docs and safe local scripts. Automated verification: go test ./..., go run ./tools/threat-coverage, git diff --check, bash tests/integration_platform_local.sh, macOS Keychain store/delete smoke, Linux cross-compile for platformauth/fd0/fd0-agent, manual provider scripts skip unless explicitly opted in. Manual hardware/UI smoke remains opt-in: FD0_PLATFORM_LOCAL_MACOS_MANUAL=1 bash tests/manual_platform_macos.sh and FD0_PLATFORM_LOCAL_LINUX_MANUAL=1 bash tests/manual_platform_linux.sh.

name: Wave D: VerifiedSTH type-state for verify-before-commit
description:
Type-state pattern: a translog.STH can ONLY be persisted into the vault
after passing VerifyAndCrossCheck. Currently this is a runtime
assertion at every call site. Make it a compile-time guarantee.

Bug pattern this eliminates: "wrong ordering" (20% of all bugs) +
"persist before verify" subset of "missing check".

## Design

```go
// internal/cli/translog.go

// VerifiedSTH proves that an STH passed full server-pub +
// inclusion + consistency + (optional) witness cross-check.
// Constructible ONLY via VerifyAndCrossCheck.
type VerifiedSTH struct {
    // private fields — no other package can construct
    sth     translog.STH
    server  CanonicalURL
    chainID ScopeID
}

func (v *VerifiedSTH) STH() translog.STH { return v.sth }
func (v *VerifiedSTH) Encode() ([]byte, error) { ... }

// Returns *VerifiedSTH only if everything verifies.
func VerifyAndCrossCheck(...) (*VerifiedSTH, error)
```

Then ScopeData.LastSTH update only via:
```go
func (sd *ScopeData) PersistLastSTH(v *VerifiedSTH) {
    sd.LastSTH, _ = v.Encode()
}
```

Calling `sd.LastSTH = encodedRawSTH` becomes a private-field violation
(or we remove the public field entirely and force going through
PersistLastSTH).

## Acceptance

- VerifiedSTH cannot be constructed outside `cli` package
- Persist functions take *VerifiedSTH, not raw STH
- A test that tries to construct VerifiedSTH externally fails to compile
  (verified by running `go build ./...` after a deliberate violation)
- All tests green

## Bug classes eliminated

- sync.go:430 "push verify proves wrong event" — caller can no longer
  hand a raw STH past verify
- "Wrong ordering: persist before verify" — compile error

## Effort

1 day. Smaller refactor than Wave C.

## Dependencies

Should land AFTER Wave C (CanonicalURL + ScopeID feed VerifiedSTH).

name: Expose item history in the desktop GUI
description:
Requested by the user 2026-07-25: see an item's previous values, like 1Password's history.

Feasible? Yes, the data already exists. NOT implementable from the renderer alone, which is why this is filed rather than built: the handoff scopes protocol changes out of the desktop UI work.

What exists today:
- Each scope is an append-only, signed event chain (internal/chain/scope.go). Every save is a new event and old events are never rewritten. internal/chain/compact.go explicitly refuses to compact because that would create unauthenticated history gaps. So prior versions of a record are still on disk and still verifiable.
- Pass items already carry a monotonic revision counter in meta (internal/passitem/passitem.go lines 83-116).

What is missing, in order:
1. A bridge method. internal/desktopbridge/service.go exposes 25 methods and none is history-shaped. Needs one taking a scope id plus record name and returning a list of revision, timestamp, author, summary; plus a way to read one past version's fields, ideally reusing the same field projection as the existing detail method so history renders through the FieldView shape the UI already knows.
2. An IPC channel and a preload allowlist entry, following the existing pattern in src/main/index.ts.
3. A history entry type in src/shared/contracts.ts and two new methods on DesktopAPI.
4. Renderer: a History section in the detail panel, or a tab beside the fields. Revealing a past secret must go through the same native confirmation and the same managed clipboard as a current one. A historical password is exactly as sensitive as the live one.

Design questions worth deciding before building:
- How far back to expose. The chain is unbounded; the UI probably wants the last N revisions with a show-more.
- Whether a past version can be restored or only read and copied. Restoring is an ordinary save of an old payload so it needs no new write path, but it does need a confirmation since it silently overwrites the current value.
- Whether history survives a vault key rotation. Removing a member rotates the key; old events should stay readable to current members, but confirm rather than assume.

Security note: this widens what the renderer can ask for. Today a compromised renderer can read current values. With history it could read every value an item ever had, including ones the user deliberately rotated away from. That is a real change in blast radius and should be a deliberate decision, not a side effect of a UI feature.
result:
Built end to end and verified against the real bridge.

Go (internal/chain, internal/cli, internal/desktopbridge):
- ReplayScope now delegates to ReplayScopeObserved, which fires an observer for every secret.set version. Every signature, sequence, prev-hash, member-set and AAD check runs exactly as before; the observer only reports what replay already computed. It is skipped at the same pre-admit early return, and the member.change projection rebuild fires nothing, so a re-encryption never shows up as a user edit.
- Three RPC methods: item.history (paged, newest first, default 50 / cap 200, with a byte budget that sets truncated rather than blowing the 1 MiB frame), item.version (same ItemDetail shape and masking as item.detail), item.restore.
- field.value gained an optional seq so a historical value is revealed through the identical code path, limits and native confirmation. Absent seq is byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- History follows the secret ID, not the name, so a rename keeps one continuous thread. A deleted item is matched by the name its last surviving version carried, and that fallback never considers live ids.
- Author labels reuse the same trusted-label index as scope.members: You, a pinned contact's label, or a short form. Never a raw fingerprint.

Restore semantics, corrected during integration: the first implementation wrote the historical payload back verbatim, which rolled the pass-item revision counter BACKWARDS - the history list showed 'Revision 4' sitting above 'Revision 5', and restoring the same version twice produced two identical numbers. Restoring rolls the content back but is still a new version, so the revision is now derived from the version being REPLACED and updated_at is set to now. Covered by TestRestoreSecretVersionAdvancesRevision.

Desktop: contracts, hardened IPC and preload entries, and a History section in the item detail - a version thread with revision, relative time, author and shape summary; View opens a past version with secrets still masked; Restore goes through a native confirmation that says the current value is replaced and stays in history. An unreadable history says so instead of claiming the item has none.

Verified: go build, go vet, full go test ./... green including simtest and wirecompat; typecheck clean; 33 unit tests; 4 e2e tests twice; package builds. Live check against the real bridge: two edits produced revisions 3-4-5, restoring revision 4 produced revision 6 with the restored content. Isolated throwaway homes only.

name: Agent: wire platform-local unlock safely
description:
Thread platform-local through fd0-agent without weakening credential handling.

Scope:
- Extend agent config with NewPlatformLocalResolver or ProviderRegistry.

name: Build fd0 desktop GUI
description:
Goal: ship fd0 as a consumer-grade desktop password manager that can be presented alongside products such as 1Password and Bitwarden, while preserving fd0-agent as the only long-lived key holder.

Product position:
- The desktop app is an end-user product, not a graphical CLI.
- A normal hosted-service user must never need a terminal, config file, server URL, agent command, internal ID, or protocol term.
- Agent lifecycle, background sync, retries, projections, updates, and socket repair happen automatically.
- Internal scopes receive a familiar user-facing concept and name, likely vaults. Internal terms such as scope, OEK, chain tip, and agent remain in diagnostics only.
- Advanced users keep the full CLI and technical diagnostics without forcing that model onto everyone else.

Desktop architecture:
- Use Electron with a hardened preload boundary and a SolidJS and TypeScript renderer.
- A versioned Go stdio bridge provides high-level application operations by reusing fd0 domain code and the existing fd0-agent crypto RPC.
- Do not move password-manager CRUD into fd0-agent and do not parse human CLI output.
- One desktop release bundle owns matching fd0, fd0-agent, and GUI versions.

Consumer first-run experience:
- Launch directly into Create, Restore, or Use existing fd0 data.
- Default to the hosted fd0 service without asking for infrastructure choices.
- Explain the passphrase and recovery implications in plain language.
- Detect an existing fd0 home automatically.
- Reach the first saved login within five minutes without documentation.
- Present recovery setup as a clear safety step and keep an actionable reminder until completed.

Everyday product experience:
- Fast global search, keyboard navigation, item detail and editing.
- Password generation, TOTP, passkeys-as-data, files, recursive sections, safe copy and timed reveal.
- Automatic sync with quiet healthy state and actionable failure state.
- Lock, auto-lock, tray/menu integration, launch at login, updates, import/export, and settings for clipboard and security behavior.
- No terminal aesthetic or developer dashboard. Use a calm, familiar three-pane password-manager layout with a dark-only theme, strong accessibility, and fd0 identity through precise trust and sharing states rather than decoration.

Initial platform scope:
- macOS arm64/amd64 and Linux amd64/arm64.
- Windows is a later milestone because current AF_UNIX agent and filesystem conventions are unvalidated.

Distribution:
- Signed or verifiable install artifacts and an explicit scripts/install.sh --gui path.
- Installing the GUI also provides matching fd0 and fd0-agent binaries with one update owner.
- Desktop bundles include YubiKey-capable binaries where platform packaging can satisfy PC/SC dependencies.

Market boundary:
- The desktop release can be marketed as fd0 Password Manager for Desktop once onboarding and daily use require no CLI.
- Direct category parity with 1Password and Bitwarden additionally requires browser autofill, save/update prompts, passkey assertion, migration importers, and later mobile integration. Track these as follow-up products instead of pretending the first desktop release already provides them.

Done when all child tasks are verified, clean-machine user tests can install, create or restore, save and retrieve credentials, sync, recover, update, and uninstall without terminal knowledge, and GUI/CLI continue to share one vault and agent safely.

name: Pure crypto layer: OpenSealedFromShared
description:
Goal: implement the post-ECDH portion of libsodium crypto_box_seal_open as a pure function that takes the ECDH shared secret as input. Verified against nacl/box's existing OpenAnonymous via property test.

Reference: nacl/box.OpenAnonymous (golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/box) is libsodium-compatible (already used by crypto.OpenAnonymous in internal/crypto/crypto.go). The construction:

  shared = X25519(card_priv, eph_pub)                 ; on-card step (input here)
  sym_key = HSalsa20(shared, zero_nonce)              ; nacl key-derive
  nonce = BLAKE2b-512(eph_pub || recipient_pub)[:24]
  plain = XSalsa20-Poly1305_open(ct, nonce, sym_key)

Steps:
1. internal/crypto/sealedbox.go: add OpenSealedFromShared(ephPub, recipientPub [32]byte, ct, shared []byte) ([]byte, bool). Returns plaintext + ok flag (matches existing OpenAnonymous signature).

2. Implementation: use golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/secretbox for the AEAD open (XSalsa20-Poly1305) and golang.org/x/crypto/salsa20/salsa for HSalsa20, and golang.org/x/crypto/blake2b for the nonce. (Same primitives nacl/box uses internally.)

3. Roundtrip property test (sealedbox_test.go):
   - Generate random recipient X25519 keypair.
   - SealAnonymous(plain, recipientPub) via existing crypto.SealAnonymous.
   - ParseSealed → eph_pub, ct.
   - shared = curve25519.X25519(recipientPriv, eph_pub).
   - plain' = OpenSealedFromShared(eph_pub, recipientPub, ct, shared).
   - Assert plain' == plain AND ok.
   - Run 200 random iterations.

4. Cross-check vectors: hard-code 3–5 sealed-box test vectors generated externally (e.g. via Python pynacl) into testdata/sealedbox_vectors.json. Includes (recipient_priv, recipient_pub, plaintext, sealed). Replay test verifies our open path on each.

5. Negative tests: tampered ct, wrong recipient pub, wrong shared, truncated input — all return ok=false.

Done when:
- OpenSealedFromShared passes 200-iter property test against existing OpenAnonymous.
- Cross-check vectors verify (proves we match libsodium, not just ourselves).
- All negative tests pass.
- Codex review confirms libsodium semantics match.
result: OpenSealedFromShared lands pure-software libsodium crypto_box_seal_open completion. HSalsa20 key derivation + BLAKE2b 24-byte nonce + XSalsa20-Poly1305 open. All-zero shared rejection at entry; Wipe()-with-KeepAlive on stack copies of shared and key. Both bool and err-returning variants. Tests: 200-iter property roundtrip vs nacl/box.OpenAnonymous, 3 frozen wire-format vectors, single-bit tamper anywhere in blob, wrong recipient pub, wrong shared, zero shared, bad-length shared, empty-plaintext edge case. Codex review 2 rounds, all P1/P2 resolved.

name: Harden platform-local auth for production
description: Fix the security review findings before platform-local auth is committed. Requirements: (1) prevent auth add/remove ReSeal failure from bricking unlock while preserving rollback protection: agent unlock may tolerate user-chain ahead only when the used wrap is still present in the latest signed auth.set and its encrypted_super_priv decrypts under the used K_unlock to the same super_priv; revoked/stale wraps must still be refused. (2) macOS provider must cryptographically/OS-bind the Keychain item release to user presence rather than relying only on a separate LocalAuthentication prompt, or claims must be reduced; preferred fix is SecAccessControl userPresence/biometry-bound item. (3) platform-local provider add/remove agent RPCs must require an unlocked agent state to reduce same-UID provider tampering/DoS. Add focused regression tests. Verify with targeted tests, race tests where useful, threat coverage, and diff check.

(1) Agent unlock now tolerates a user-chain-ahead AuthTip only when the used wrap is still live in the latest signed auth.set and encrypted_super_priv decrypts under the used K_unlock to the same super_priv; revoked/stale wraps still fail. Added regression tests for allowed chain-ahead recovery and revoked-method rejection. (2) macOS provider now attempts to store K_unlock in a device-local Keychain item protected by user-presence access control and fails closed with a clear entitlement/signing error instead of enrolling a weaker method when the build cannot create protected Keychain items. Manual macOS smoke now requires a signed/entitled fd0-agent instead of building an impossible unsigned temp agent. (3) PlatformLocalAdd/Rm agent RPCs now require the agent to be unlocked before provider state is touched. Verification: go test ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/platformauth ./internal/vault ./internal/chain ./internal/server/validate passed; bash tests/integration_platform_local.sh passed; shell syntax and non-opt-in manual script skips passed; go test -race ./internal/agent ./internal/platformauth ./internal/vault passed; go test ./... passed; go run ./tools/threat-coverage passed; git diff --check passed. Executive assessment: the app is functionally complete but reads as an MVP for three structural reasons, not cosmetic ones.
1. Navigation hides the product. Every item type sits behind one dropdown in the sidebar; default filter is 'password'.
2. State is invisible. Filters AND together silently with no chip and no clear affordance; errors are a single raw string slot; empty states are dead ends.
3. There is no design system. Measured: 16 independent button implementations, 71 colors in use against 17 tokens, 33 spacing values with no scale, 14 font sizes, 10 font weights, 8 radii, 10 ad-hoc z-index values.

Non-goals: no light theme, no cloning another product's identity, no browser autofill/importers/passkey assertion in this release.

Shell: command palette (Cmd+K) that searches items and runs commands in one surface, with Cmd+Enter to copy a password without opening the item; icon rail for item types; vault as a title-bar context switcher; inline copy actions on list rows.

Foundation: ui/tokens.css plus a primitive set (Button, Field family, Popover, Menu, Modal, notices). App.tsx went from a 1889-line monolith to a shell over lib/ (state, errors, formatting) and features/ (one file per surface). styles.css was rebuilt on tokens.

Verification, all against isolated throwaway homes — production ~/.fd0 and its agent were never touched: typecheck clean, 33 unit tests pass, 4 e2e tests pass (up from 3, including new coverage for the clipped-popover regression, overlay Escape ordering, the command palette, filter chips, and first run), bun run package succeeds. Visually checked at 1440/1024/900/860/700/560 with zero horizontal overflow and no console errors.

Three bugs found during the work and fixed: drag-and-drop in the password editor (drop slots must keep a non-zero resting height or the controller discards them), toasts intercepting clicks meant for modals, and popovers painting under modals.

One backend blocker found and NOT fixed, as it is out of scope for the desktop UI: the vault locks itself about 1.5s after creation. Filed as ncc144aq with a reproduction. Nothing is committed.

name: Close the accessibility gaps
description:
P1. ARIA coverage is genuinely good - roles on every modal and menu, live regions, drag-and-drop announcements, keyboard drag, and a global amber focus ring at 10.7:1 (styles.css:82-87). The gaps are specific.

Focus:
- outline:0 appears 7x. Four override the global ring by equal specificity and later source order. Three have no replacement at all: .generator-controls select (styles.css:1158), .onboarding-main input (:1424), .json-editor textarea (:2626). Confirmed by logging the tab order in the running window - the search input reports 'outline: 0px none' while every other control shows the 2px amber ring.
- textarea is missing from the global :focus-visible list.
- No modal traps focus or restores it to the trigger on close.
- The switch input is visually hidden with pointer-events:none and the visible track has no focus style.
- Focus-indicator contrast: #7e6221 against the unfocused border #383e39 is 1.91:1 - the change is nearly invisible.

Contrast:
- --faint (#656c66) measures 3.06-3.64:1 depending on surface and is used 14x, always on 8-11px text: search placeholder, kbd chip, sidebar section labels, all counts, empty states, kind badges, field type labels. All below AA.
- Opacity-based disabled states land at 2.08-3.43:1.
- Every border in the app is below the 3:1 UI-boundary threshold; no form control has a perceivable outline.

Keyboard:
- The item list is a flat set of buttons with no listbox/option roles, no aria-selected, no arrow-key navigation, no roving tabindex.
- The TypePicker listbox has no aria-activedescendant and no arrow handling.
- Both context menus close on pointerdown only - no Escape, no focus return.
- Only the hardcoded mac glyph 'CmdF' is surfaced; the other shortcuts exist solely in the menu bar.
result:
One focus ring, declared once and never removed. The search field's missing ring is gone with the field itself (it is now a button that opens the palette); no rule in the new stylesheet sets outline:0 without a replacement.

Modals trap focus, restore it to the trigger on close, and confirm before discarding a dirty form. The item list is a real listbox with options, aria-selected, roving tabindex, and Home/End/arrow navigation. Menus and the palette have arrow-key navigation and return focus on close.

Contrast: --text-4 (5.2:1 on the base surface, 4.9:1 at worst) replaces the failing --faint; --line-control gives controls a perceivable boundary; disabled states desaturate instead of dropping to 2-3:1 via opacity. Field labels no longer concatenate into 'Notesoptional' for anything reading label text directly.

Shortcuts are now discoverable: Cmd+/ opens a full list, and the palette footer names its own keys.

name: Create selection contrast mockups
description: Create three isolated HTML mockups using the current fd0 Desktop information architecture and fixed pure-white workspace/dark frame. Compare only the selected-row treatment: A restrained amber wash, B outline-only, and C softened graphite. Keep typography, spacing, content, and surrounding colors constant so the selection contrast is the only meaningful variable. Provide direct visual comparison, concise token labels, and launch locally without changing production Desktop code. Acceptance: valid standalone HTML, all three concepts visible at desktop width, screenshot visually inspected, and local gallery opened for user review.
result: Rebuilt the standalone HTML gallery as a controlled A/B/C comparison using the current fd0 Desktop shell. Added Amber Wash, Outline only, and Soft Graphite selected-row treatments while keeping the pure-white workspace, dark frame, layout, content, and brand palette constant. Verified three rendered concepts, exact computed selection colors, no browser console warnings/errors, visual screenshots for every direction, and git diff whitespace checks. Production Desktop code was not changed.

name: Add notes as a first-class pass-item field
description:
Approved by the user 2026-07-25 while deciding the item-editor direction: notes should be part of the schema rather than a convention.

Why top-level rather than a new field type: there is exactly one notes per item, it has no name that could be renamed, it cannot be nested into a section or duplicated, and it is not a credential. A field named "notes" by convention has none of those guarantees.

  internal/passitem/passitem.go
    Item.Notes string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
    MaxNotesBytes = 8 * 1024

`omitempty` keeps every item written before this existed byte-identical on the wire. Validate trims trailing whitespace and enforces the cap independently of MaxItemBytes, so a long note fails with a message about notes rather than about the item being too large.

Wire risk checked, not assumed: internal/wirecompat covers the vault and chain formats, not the pass-item payload, which travels as opaque JSON inside the encrypted body. Full `go test ./...` including wirecompat and simtest passes.

Bridge: projected in detailFields as a FieldView with path `$notes`, type `notes`, in its own trailing "Notes" section - mirroring how `$url` is handled. field.value resolves `$notes` the same way it resolves `$url`.

Deliberately NOT in the inventory summary. The subtitle stays website-or-username. Inventory is a bulk projection held in renderer memory for every item at once; note text can be far more sensitive than a hostname and has no business being in a list payload.

Desktop: PassItemData gains an optional notes; the editor shows a Notes textarea for password items; the detail renders notes as prose - full width, `white-space: pre-wrap` so line breaks survive, and no repeated label, because a "Notes" row inside a "NOTES" section said the same thing twice.

Verified end to end against the real bridge: typed a two-line note, saved, the detail shows both lines, reopening the editor round-trips the value. Plus unit tests for round trip, omission when empty, whitespace trimming, the size limit, and an old item without notes still decoding.
result: Superseded by iughu3gt: the top-level property was measured to cause silent data loss when an older client writes the item back. Notes are now a reserved text field instead.

name: Prevent sync status layout shift
description: Keep the titlebar search position stable while the sync button label changes between its idle and 'Syncing…' states. Reserve a fixed desktop-width slot for the sync control, retain the compact icon-only responsive state below 900px, and add a focused layout assertion.
result: Reserved a 104px desktop sync-control slot and retained the compact icon-only control below 900px. Electron layout coverage swaps the label to Syncing and proves the palette left edge and button width do not change. Five Electron journeys passed.

name: Gate desktop onboarding on sync and verified recovery
description:
Severity: P1 data-safety release blocker.

Problem:
The desktop app creates the identity and first vault immediately, then allows users to save items. Recovery export is hidden in Settings and no persistent state records that recovery was completed. A recovery file restores the identity only; scope history must be fetched from the server. Unsynced local items are therefore not recoverable after device loss even when the user exported the identity recovery file.

Required approach:
- Model onboarding as resumable states: identity created, official server trusted, first sync complete, recovery exported, recovery verified, ready.
- Do not claim data is protected or backed up before a successful server sync.
- Present recovery setup as a first-class safety step and retain a visible actionable reminder until verified.
- Verify the exported recovery artifact without exposing key material, and explain precisely that it restores identity while server sync restores vault contents.
- Make partial create/scope failures idempotently resumable rather than requiring deletion or a terminal.
- Preserve offline use deliberately: users may continue with a clear local-only risk state, never a false healthy state.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clean create and restore flows survive cancellation, app crash, network loss, duplicate retry, and partial scope creation.
- A user cannot mistake an unsynced vault for a recoverable vault.
- Recovery export/import plus server sync is tested end to end on a clean home.
- Existing recovery files and v1 vault data remain usable.
- No remediation step tells users to delete an existing vault or user chain.
result: Added resumable desktop readiness state for first successful sync and verified recovery export. Recovery files are exported by the bridge, decrypted and matched to the current identity, written atomically with mode 0600, and only then marked complete. Restore marks identity recovery while a separate sync remains required for vault contents. The GUI keeps an explicit local-only/recovery warning until both steps complete. Verified cryptographic tamper tests, readiness persistence, Desktop E2E export/restore, and isolated non-TTY first sync.

name: Build hardened desktop shell
description:
Part of fd0 desktop GUI. Build the hardened Electron desktop shell with a SolidJS and TypeScript renderer.

Selected stack:
- Electron main process with a hardened preload boundary.
- SolidJS and TypeScript renderer.
- Bundled Go stdio bridge connected to the existing fd0-agent.
- Deno Desktop is not on the first-release critical path.

Required boundaries:
- Load only packaged local assets.
- Keep renderer code unable to open arbitrary files, sockets, subprocesses, or network destinations.
- Expose one typed, validated application operation per allowed binding.
- Deny unexpected navigation, windows, webviews, permissions, and shell/file access.
- Main/backend owns and supervises the bundled Go bridge; renderer never invokes raw CLI commands.
- Present native menus, tray integration, app lifecycle, launch-at-login, deep links, and update states as product features rather than developer controls.

Done when:
- Development and production builds launch on macOS and Linux.
- Security configuration and binding allow-lists are covered by tests and static checks.
- Renderer compromise cannot invoke arbitrary backend operations.
- Bridge crash, restart, and incompatible versions recover through end-user-safe UI.
- The shell supports the dark-only theme, accessibility, keyboard navigation, compact windows, and packaged-app E2E.
result: Implemented the hardened Electron/Solid shell with context isolation, sandboxing, no Node integration, strict CSP, custom local protocol, denied navigation/windows/permissions, explicit preload bindings, Electron fuses, native macOS inset controls, menus, tray, launch-at-login, shortcuts, updater UI, responsive E2E, and bridge crash recovery. Deep links remain intentionally deferred to the browser-integration product so no unused attack surface ships.

name: Make agent lock and auth revocation authoritative
description: Release blocker from the deep security review. Findings: FD0-025, FD0-026, FD0-027. Revoke existing SSH-agent signing sessions on lock/expiry, derive rollback references from trusted local state instead of caller input, and reject or garbage-collect orphan auth wraps outside the signed auth chain. Add live-connection lock, revoked-method rollback, and orphan-wrap tests. Evidence: /Users/valentinkolb/.codex/security-scans/fd0.sh/1343f819-5298-4d9d-a152-2dd6cd132768/report.md.
result: Made canonical agent-owned vault/user-chain paths authoritative; every unlock now validates the used wrap against the current signed auth.set, rejecting revoked and legacy orphan credentials. Auth enrollment authorizes the method in the chain before persisting its wrap with a compensating rollback path. Existing SSH protocol connections re-fetch live keys for every list/sign operation, so explicit lock and expiry revoke signing immediately. No wire fields or vault formats changed. Verified go test ./...; go test -race ./internal/agent; focused agent/CLI/vault tests; isolated filesystem integration 15/15; relevant multi-device auth add/unlock/remove/revocation checks all passed. Unrelated stale route/YubiKey assertions in broader integrations remain outside this task.

name: Define one bundle and update ownership model
description:
Part of fd0 desktop GUI. Package GUI, fd0, and fd0-agent as one version-aligned desktop product.

Approach:
- Embed matching standard or YubiKey-capable Go binaries in the signed desktop bundle.
- Provide stable CLI entry points from ~/.local/bin that resolve into the installed desktop bundle, with no second independently updated copy.
- Teach fd0 update to detect desktop-managed installs and hand off to the desktop updater or print an exact action instead of mutating signed app contents.
- Add scripts/install.sh --gui while retaining CLI-only installation as the default.
- Define idempotent install, upgrade, flavor, uninstall, PATH, desktop-entry, and rollback behavior for macOS and Linux.
- Keep existing CLI-only release/update behavior intact.

Done when:
- GUI install also makes fd0 and fd0-agent available and version-matched.
- GUI auto-update or upgrade updates all three together and running-agent restart is handled.
- Re-running install.sh --gui is idempotent.
- CLI-only and desktop-managed upgrade tests pass without broken symlinks or mixed versions.
result: Implemented one Desktop-owned distribution: signed app bundle embeds version-matched YubiKey-capable fd0, fd0-agent, and bridge; installers create managed wrappers; Linux relays commands into the current AppImage; bundled fd0 update hands off to Support; updates stop the old agent before replacement; uninstall preserves ~/.fd0; installer and packaged relay tests pass.

name: Diagnose doctor auto-unlock timeout
description: Read-only follow-up for local fd0 0.1.1. Reproduce from supplied output: agent status reports unlocked, then fd0 doctor invokes automatic passphrase unlock and times out. Inspect command preflight, agent RPC deadlines, current unlocked timestamp, and safe runtime state. Do not restart, unlock, modify vault/config/services, or run UI tests. Deliver immediate guidance and refine the bug-fix proposal with acceptance criteria.
result: Read-only follow-up completed. The failed doctor caused a second successful late unlock: unlocked_since moved from 2026-07-27 18:37:09 CEST to 18:44:12 CEST. Public vault-header metadata is normal (one passphrase wrap, Argon2 64 MiB / 3 iterations / p=1; two wraps total). The installed arm64 Desktop agent runs at macOS priority 4 while the shell and isolated dev agent run at 31. Its bundled SMAppService plist explicitly sets ProcessType=Background, which launchd throttles; this is the concrete cause of slow interactive Argon2. A separate 15s RPC design still converts late success into raw timeout. Doctor is also in the auto-unlock command set and status does not refresh the default 5m idle deadline, explaining the surprise prompt around expiry. Proposed immediate terminal-agent workaround and three surgical fixes: use Standard/Interactive service classification, dedicated unlock deadline/late-success handling, and doctor no-auto-unlock/status-error handling. No source, vault, config, service, agent, or UI state changed.

name: Remove hidden Linux desktop runtime dependencies
description:
Severity: P1 release blocker for Linux GUI-only users.

Problem:
The Linux desktop always bundles YubiKey-capable binaries. DEB/RPM declare PCSC runtime dependencies, while AppImage does not prove that the bundled agent runs without host PCSC libraries. Linux in-app update verification shells out to cosign, which a GUI-only user will normally not have. The current AppImage build also uses electron-builder legacy FUSE2 runtime by default.

Required approach:
- Make standard GUI create, unlock, sync, and update work with zero manually installed tools or libraries.
- Determine and document the fd0-agent dynamic library closure for x64 and arm64.
- Prefer isolating YubiKey/PIV support behind a loadable or bundled helper so passphrase users are not coupled to PCSC; otherwise bundle and verify a compatible runtime with licensing accounted for.
- Replace external cosign invocation with an embedded, auditable verifier and pinned release identity while retaining checksum and signature verification.
- Evaluate electron-builder AppImage toolset 1.0.3 static runtime on the supported distro matrix; use DEB/RPM as the primary path if the beta runtime is not stable enough.
- Fail YubiKey capability checks clearly without breaking standard vault access.

Acceptance criteria:
- AppImage runs and updates on clean supported distributions without cosign, FUSE2, PCSC, or terminal setup for standard use.
- DEB/RPM dependency installation and removal are correct.
- YubiKey available/unavailable states are tested separately.
- Update verification still rejects wrong architecture, manifest, certificate identity, checksum, downgrade, and tampered payload.
- x64 and arm64 clean-machine tests cover Ubuntu, Fedora/Rocky, and one rolling or minimal distribution.
result: Removed hidden Linux runtime dependencies. AppImage uses toolset 1.0.3, bundles libpcsclite.so.1 and license for YubiKey-capable binaries, and uses the bundled Sigstore verifier instead of host Cosign. DEB/RPM dependencies and safe removal hooks are explicit. Release CI covers x64/arm64 native AppImage relays plus Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Rocky 9, passphrase unlock without host PCSC, ldd closure, and package install/removal. Locally verified an actual arm64 AppImage/DEB/RPM build and clean-container runtime. Desktop unit/E2E, installer integration, packaging, codesign verification, ShellCheck, Actionlint, Go tests/vet, and audit pass.

name: Harden SSH key references and projection refresh
description: Make host key lookup vault-scoped, reject nonexistent or non-key references on Desktop host save, and invoke the shared SSH projection refresh after Desktop host/key writes and removals. Add focused Go tests, including duplicate key names across vaults.
result: Vault-scoped key resolution, reference validation, and projection refresh implemented and tested.

name: Agent API: shared unlock surface for CLI and GUI
description:
Make fd0-agent the single shared authority for platform-local unlock so CLI and future GUI use the same security boundary.

Scope:
- Add/extend agent RPC so clients can request platform-local unlock and query provider capabilities without learning K_unlock or super_priv.
- CLI and GUI remain thin clients: they select method/provider and display errors, but decrypted identity material stays inside fd0-agent.
- If an OS requires a foreground UI context, prefer an agent-owned/signed platform helper over returning K_unlock to the GUI. The helper may show native UI and returns K_unlock only to the agent over a private channel.
- Define provider capability response: available, enrolled, policy support, needs GUI/foreground, setup hint.
- Keep existing fd0-agent lifecycle semantics: one local agent per FD0_HOME, mlocked super_priv, lock wipes memory, status exposes active method id but not secrets.

Acceptance:
- GUI can unlock by calling agent RPC, not by reimplementing vault open.
- CLI and GUI share the same method selection, diagnostics, and fallback behavior.
- No GUI code path receives K_unlock, payload_key, or super_priv unless explicitly accepted in a later security decision.
- Tests cover fake GUI/client RPC flow and verify agent remains the only process caching unlocked identity material.
result: Shared unlock surface is in place: agent RPC accepts method_type=platform-local, CLI sends no K_unlock or provider secret, and future GUI can call the same Unlock operation. Provider-capability querying is deferred to real macOS/Linux provider tasks because dev-local exposes only opt-in test availability.

name: Package the PTY runtime
description: Add pinned @xterm/xterm, @xterm/addon-fit, and node-pty dependencies. Keep node-pty external to the main bundle, rebuild it for Electron 43, unpack its native binary from ASAR where required, and extend macOS arm64/x64 plus Linux arm64/x64 release jobs with packaged PTY smoke checks.
result: Pinned xterm/FitAddon/node-pty, externalized and unpacked node-pty, added macOS/Linux x64+arm64 release PTY smokes, and verified the final packaged macOS arm64 native runtime.

name: Integrate agent lifecycle and shared local state
description:
Part of fd0 desktop GUI. Make GUI and CLI coexist against one FD0_HOME and one fd0-agent.

Approach:
- GUI detects, starts, unlocks, locks, stops, and restarts the existing agent using the same lifecycle semantics as fd0.
- Resolve the bundled fd0-agent explicitly instead of PATH lookup.
- Respect idle timeout, max lifetime, default auth method, YubiKey policy, background sync, vault flock, and SSH-agent socket behavior.
- Add filesystem/state notifications through polling or bridge events without bypassing the existing lock.
- Handle another CLI command or auto-sync holding the vault lock with progress and retry UX.
- Verify a terminal fd0 process and the GUI see each other's writes after replay/sync.

Done when:
- No duplicate/orphan agent can be created by GUI + CLI races.
- Version/flavor mismatch is detected before unlock.
- Integration tests cover GUI first launch, existing unlocked agent, stale sockets, restart, concurrent CLI use, idle lock, and YubiKey capability states.
result: Implemented shared fd0 home and agent lifecycle behavior for production plus fully isolated development. Desktop starts/unlocks/locks/restarts the explicit bundled agent, detects version/flavor drift, repairs stale PID/socket state, polls lock state, honors existing auth/default method and sync config, and keeps real CLI/SSH state untouched during development verification.

name: C1: BENCH.md add 100k bench data
description: Append 100k AppendLeaf / Inclusion / Consistency Proof figures (already collected) to BENCH.md, replace the linear extrapolation with real numbers, note the SQL-cache-loss inflection at 10k→100k. ~5 min, edit one file.
result: BENCH.md erweitert mit 100k-Datenpunkten + revised extrapolation. 2 commits (88dbca4 + 72f24ef für codex P2 fixes). Insight: SQL-Cache spillt bei ~10k → 100k, AppendLeaf 9× langsamer für 10× scale. >100k events/chain ist v1.0 nicht komfortabel — Wave H tracks horizontal partitioning option.

name: Wire decomposition into yubikey_piv.go
result: OpenSealedBox(card, sealed) free function wires the decomposition. Plain-nil + typed-nil Card guards (reflect-based, catches the Go gotcha). Layer errors wrapped with descriptive prefixes. Shared secret Wiped on every return. Tests: MockCard roundtrip + 100-iter property test (no tag); pivWrapper pending-hardware error pinning + length-check-before-hardware (-tags=yubikey). The only remaining hardware-day TODO is the body of pivWrapper.SharedSecret. Codex review: 2 rounds, all P1/P2 resolved.

commit.message: yubikey: free-function OpenSealedBox wires Card into the open path (subtask 4)

name: Fix desktop dev CSS and local macOS package launch
description: Make the dev-only CSP compatible with Vite CSS/HMR without weakening production CSP, and ensure a locally packaged macOS fd0.app receives a valid ad-hoc signature after Electron fuse mutation so Spotlight launches do not crash. Verify both paths without touching ~/.fd0.
result: Added a serve-only Vite CSP transform so dev CSS/HMR load while production CSP remains strict. Added a local package wrapper that ad-hoc signs and verifies macOS bundles after Electron fuse changes. Verified typecheck, unit tests 2/2, Electron E2E 2/2, computed dev styles in Chrome, strict production CSP, codesign verification, CLI relay, isolated packaged GUI smoke, Spotlight indexing, and unchanged production fd0 state.

name: Harden browser autofill after release review
description: Resolve every validated robustness finding from the independent browser autofill review. Scope: form/account targeting, MV3 reinjection and frame-scoped lifecycle state, idempotent native mutations, canonical credential field updates/TOTP replacement, release packaging, Chromium registration, docs/skill truthfulness, accessibility/cache/concurrency hardening, and real headless MV3 integration coverage. Preserve strict HTTPS/origin/revision boundaries and avoid production fd0 data. Done when focused browser and Go regressions pass, a packaged host is present, headless Chrome exercises the built extension lifecycle, desktop/website builds remain green, and no visible Electron test or production vault is used.
result: Resolved all validated review findings across form/account targeting, MV3 lifecycle and frame state, mutation idempotency, canonical nested fields, packaging, docs, Chromium support and test coverage. Full Go suite, 47 browser tests plus real MV3 smoke, 62 Desktop tests/build, isolated installer, website build, vet, audits, policy and GoReleaser checks are green.

name: Make first-contact sync work safely in the desktop app
description:
Severity: P0 release blocker.

Problem:
The desktop bridge implements sync.run by calling the interactive CLI sync path. On first contact, EnsurePinnedServer requires a TTY confirmation unless FD0_AUTO_PIN=1. The stdio desktop bridge is not a TTY, so a GUI-only user can create or restore a vault but cannot complete the first hosted sync. Globally enabling FD0_AUTO_PIN would silently remove the safety-number ceremony and is not acceptable.

Required approach:
- Define a non-interactive, typed bridge operation for first-contact server inspection and pinning instead of parsing CLI prompts.
- For the official hosted fd0 service, establish a release-bound trust anchor: ship the expected canonical server identity or an authenticated key-transition mechanism in the signed desktop release, verify the fetched server-info signature, and pin only on an exact match.
- For custom servers, show the canonical URL, verified server identity, and safety fingerprint in a native confirmation dialog before persisting the pin.
- Bind preview and commit to the same canonical URL and public key so the confirmation cannot race a changed server response.
- Keep FD0_AUTO_PIN limited to explicit test/operator automation.
- Map all first-contact failures to actionable GUI messages without protocol jargon.

Acceptance criteria:
- A clean GUI-only install can create or restore, pin the official server, register the user, and complete its first sync without a terminal.
- A custom server requires explicit native confirmation.
- Key mismatch, changed response, malformed server-info, offline startup, cancellation, and retry are covered.
- Automated tests prove non-TTY first contact without weakening CLI pinning policy.
- Existing pinned servers and vault data remain compatible.
result: Implemented structured first-contact sync with verified server preview, native trust confirmation for custom services, pinned hosted-service identity, preview/commit race protection, exact-server sync binding, and isolated non-TTY integration coverage. Verified Go tests, Desktop typecheck/unit/E2E, and isolated sync without changing the production fd0 instance.

name: Address review findings for fd0 SSH and render fixes
description: Apply the review findings from the SSH socket and single-context render fix review. Scope: fd0 ssh <alias> should preflight the fd0 SSH-agent socket for every fd0-rendered host, not only hosts with KeyName; kube/talos RenderInput comments must describe singleton default current-context behavior; add focused sim coverage for fd0 ssh <alias> with a refusing/stale FD0_SSH_SOCK so the clear fd0 error is asserted before ssh exec. Acceptance: targeted tests, go test ./..., go vet ./..., and git diff --check pass.
result: Addressed all review findings. fd0 ssh <alias> now preflights the fd0 SSH-agent socket for every fd0-rendered host before execing ssh; kube/talos RenderInput comments document the singleton current/active context default; added sim coverage proving fd0 ssh <alias> reports a refusing FD0_SSH_SOCK and does not exec ssh. Verification: gofmt, targeted sim and renderer tests, git diff --check, go test ./..., and go vet ./... all pass. Changes remain uncommitted.

name: Publish standard and yubikey client release archives
description:
Extend .goreleaser.yaml and GitHub release workflow to publish two client archive flavors.

Requirements:
- Keep existing standard archive names for compatibility: fd0_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz.
- Add YubiKey archive names: fd0_yubikey_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz.
- YubiKey archives contain binaries named fd0 and fd0-agent, not fd0-yubikey, so installed commands stay stable.
- Standard builds remain CGO_ENABLED=0 where possible.
- YubiKey builds use -tags=netgo,yubikey and the required cgo/PCSC environment.
- Preserve checksum and cosign verification model.

Acceptance:
- CI compile job still verifies -tags=yubikey.
- Release dry-run or snapshot proves both archive name families exist.
- checksums.txt includes all standard and yubikey archives.
result: Release workflow now publishes fd0_yubikey client archives and merges them into checksums.

name: Build fd0 browser autofill integration
description:
Future product milestone required before fd0 is positioned as a full alternative to 1Password or Bitwarden rather than a desktop-only password manager.

Goal:
Ship browser integration that lets normal users save, update, find, autofill, and use credentials without copying them manually.

Architecture:
- Browser extension talks to the versioned fd0 desktop bridge through a narrowly scoped native-messaging host.
- The extension never reads vault files or talks directly to fd0-agent.
- Pair extension and desktop app explicitly and show a human-verifiable trust phrase.
- Reuse canonical URL matching and passitem metadata from fd0.
- Keep unlock authority and long-lived private keys in fd0-agent.

Product scope:
- Chrome/Chromium and Firefox first; Safari follows through its platform-specific signed extension packaging.
- Suggest matching logins for the current origin.
- Manual autofill first; inline suggestions only after security review.
- Save new login and update changed credentials.
- Generate and fill passwords.
- Fill TOTP and support passkey creation/assertion through WebAuthn interception when the browser APIs and security review permit it.
- Domain exclusions, exact/base-domain matching policy, iframe warnings, HTTP/HTTPS downgrade protection, and clipboard fallback.
- Locked state opens a consumer unlock flow in the desktop app.

Security requirements:
- Strict origin and frame validation.
- Never autofill into unrelated origins or untrusted iframes.
- No automatic fill on page load by default.
- Native-messaging requests use a versioned allow-list and carry no arbitrary command, path, or shell primitive.
- Threat model covers malicious pages, compromised extension context, confused deputy, phishing domains, and desktop/extension pairing takeover.

Done when:
- A non-technical user can install the extension, pair it, unlock fd0, save a login, revisit the site, autofill credentials and TOTP, and update the password without using the desktop item editor or CLI.
- E2E tests cover matching, lookalike domains, iframes, HTTP downgrade, multiple accounts, locked state, pairing revocation, and malformed native messages.
- Website and onboarding present browser installation as part of the normal password-manager setup.

name: Preserve desktop secret reveal across detail refreshes
description: Fix GitHub issue #19: native dialog focus refresh remounts ItemDetail and clears revealed secrets before 15 seconds. Bind lifecycle to record identity and verify refresh, expiry, and clearing with synthetic component tests only. Do not launch Electron, fd0 binaries, agents, or access production vault. No commit or release.
result: Confirmed issue #19 with a synthetic ItemDetail component test: a same-item refresh at 500 ms cleared the secret before the fix. Key the detail component by item ID instead of detail object; preserve reveal state across focus/TOTP refreshes, clear on projection changes, and ignore reveal responses after disposal. Four isolated Chromium component tests pass (13 assertions), covering the 15-second deadline, delayed confirmation, detail clearing/item switches and late responses. name: Add SFTP file transfer to fd0 CLI and Desktop
description:
Goal: add robust two-way file transfer for fd0-managed SSH hosts through a public fd0 sftp CLI and a polished Desktop Files window.

Approved CLI contract:
- fd0 sftp <host> opens an interactive native SFTP session.
- fd0 sftp ls <host> [remote-path]
- fd0 sftp tree <host> [remote-path] --depth N
- fd0 sftp stat <host> <remote-path>
- fd0 sftp cp <host> <source> <destination>, with exactly one side prefixed by remote:.
- fd0 sftp mkdir, mv, and rm complete the small remote-management surface.
- --scope follows fd0 ssh semantics; structured commands support --json where meaningful.
- Human progress is written only to stderr so stdout remains scriptable.

Architecture:
- Reuse native OpenSSH for host configuration, fd0-agent authentication, ProxyJump, Known Hosts, and platform compatibility.
- Start the trusted SSH binary with argv, never a shell, and request the SFTP subsystem.
- Speak SFTP through a small shared Go transport used by public CLI operations and a private framed Desktop helper protocol.
- Desktop main owns sessions, native dialogs, local paths, transfer lifecycle, and cancellation. The sandboxed renderer receives typed metadata and progress only and never parses CLI text or handles file bytes.

Desktop product scope:
- Add a Files action to SSH hosts and open a dedicated secondary window with the same host identity, native window treatment, light/dark themes, and one fd0 app icon.
- Provide remote breadcrumbs, listing, refresh, upload picker and drag-and-drop, download save dialog, progress, cancellation, overwrite confirmation, directory creation, rename, and confirmed delete.
- Keep the browser remote-focused; do not build a second local filesystem pane.

Security and reliability:
- Never auto-accept unknown host keys. Return an actionable instruction to verify a new host in the terminal first.
- GUI transfers require non-interactive fd0 key or agent authentication; no password storage or renderer password handling.
- No shell interpolation. Bound protocol messages and metadata, sanitize diagnostics, handle hostile filenames, avoid recursive symlink traversal, and clean temporary files after failure or cancellation.
- Preserve existing SSH terminal behavior and immutable fd0 cryptographic boundaries.

Initial platforms: macOS arm64 and x64, Linux arm64 and x64. Windows remains out of scope.

Non-goals: filesystem mounting, bidirectional synchronization, background transfers after fd0 exits, remote editing, checksum-based sync, resumable transfers, a local two-pane file manager, or replacing OpenSSH.

Done when CLI and Desktop use the shared transport, exact-byte upload and download work through direct and ProxyJump hosts, destructive actions require explicit confirmation, cancellation and overwrite behavior are deterministic, isolated tests touch no real fd0 or SSH state, packaged macOS and Linux builds include everything required, and user documentation covers workflows and limitations. Release publication remains a separately authorized step.

Website and agent skill:
- Update the public website SSH documentation and appropriate product surfaces with the released CLI and Desktop Files workflows, safe examples, limitations, metadata, and a final reviewed screenshot.
- Update the repository-owned skills/fd0 skill, its focused references, and evaluations so agents correctly use fd0 sftp for browsing and two-way transfer with safe overwrite and destructive-operation behavior.
- Treat website source and repository skill updates as required before release readiness. Deployment and publishing remain separate authorization gates.
result: Completed the approved SFTP epic: OpenSSH-backed transport, public fd0 sftp CLI, private bounded Desktop bridge, dedicated two-way Files window, transfer safety/cancellation/reconnect lifecycle, package integration, tests, website documentation, and repository fd0 skill updates. All local delivery checks passed; publication and cross-platform CI remain separate release actions.

name: YubiKey sealed-box completion (no-hardware portion)
description:
Goal: do everything possible without a YubiKey now, so hardware day shrinks to 30min: connect card, run recorder, commit JSON.

Strategy: decompose the sealed-box open path so the hardware step is one isolated call:

  card.SharedSecret(ephPub) → shared

- internal/crypto/crypto.go already has SealAnonymous + OpenAnonymous via golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/box, libsodium-compatible.

  1. Decompose: parseSealed + Card interface + MockCard
  2. Pure crypto layer: OpenSealedFromShared (matches nacl/box semantics)
  3. Golden-vector fixture format + loader + replay test
  4. Wire decomposition into yubikey_piv.go (SharedSecret stays TODO)
  5. Recorder tool scaffold (cmd/fd0-yubikey-record, behind -tags=yubikey)

Done = software CI is green; hardware day = run recorder, commit JSON, replace SharedSecret stub with one real PIV ECDH call.
result: All 5 subtasks shipped. The YubiKey sealed-box completion is now 80% done before hardware ever connects: pure crypto path (HSalsa20 + BLAKE2b nonce + XSalsa20-Poly1305 open) verified against nacl/box and frozen wire-format vectors; Card abstraction with MockCard for software-only end-to-end tests; golden-vector fixture format + loader with strict validation; pivWrapper now satisfies Card with the only hardware-day TODO being SharedSecret's ECDH call; recorder binary with self-check + atomic write fully tested via MockCard. name: Analyze configurable terminal launcher for SSH hosts

name: Build the Desktop SSH Files window
description:
Build the polished remote file browser for fd0-managed SSH hosts on top of the typed Desktop SFTP bridge.

Entry and window model:
- Add a Files action next to Open in terminal for SSH host details and relevant menus.
- Open a dedicated secondary Electron window under the existing fd0 app identity. Its title and header clearly identify <host> and Files.
- Match the established inset macOS controls, light and dark themes, spacing, focus behavior, and window lifecycle without changing the main app layout.

Browser experience:
- Show the remote current path as clickable breadcrumbs with Up, Back or history where useful, Refresh, and deterministic directories-first sorting.
- Present name, type, size, modified time, permissions when available, and clear loading, empty, disconnected, permission-denied, missing-SFTP, and locked-vault states.
- Open directories by click or keyboard; never execute remote files.
- Upload files or folders through native selection and drag-and-drop. Download through a native save or directory dialog.
- Show a compact transfer queue with per-transfer progress, current filename, completion, failure, retry, and cancel.
- Confirm overwrite, recursive transfer, rename, and delete. Destructive confirmation names the exact remote target.
- Support mkdir and rename without adding remote editing, preview, mounting, or a local two-pane browser.

Accessibility and robustness:
- Full keyboard navigation, visible focus, screen-reader names, reduced-motion compatibility, and no layout shifts when scrollbars or progress appear.
- Hostile or control-character filenames are rendered safely and remain operable.
- Window close during a transfer produces deterministic cancellation rather than a confusing global error.

Verification:
- Component tests cover navigation and operation state machines without opening Electron windows.
- CI Electron tests use isolated fake SFTP data for browse, upload, download, overwrite, cancellation, reconnect, mkdir, rename, delete confirmation, keyboard navigation, and both themes.
- Do not use real fd0 data, SSH configuration, or remote servers in tests.
result: Added a dedicated themed Files BrowserWindow for fd0 SSH hosts with breadcrumb navigation, stable scrolling, file metadata, native picker upload/download, preload-only drag/drop path resolution, folders, rename, confirmed delete, visible transfer states, progress, cancellation, refresh, light/dark styling, and SSH-host entry actions.

name: Flatten navigation and make filter state visible
description:
P0. Verified in the running window.

Navigation: all five item types sit behind one dropdown (App.tsx:1079-1136). Opened, it overlays the Views and Vaults sections. Default typeFilter is 'password' (App.tsx:102), so a user holding only Kubernetes/Talos items lands on 'No matching items'.

Filters: onVault sets vaultFilter but leaves typeFilter untouched (App.tsx:435-438) while title() derives only from mainView/typeFilter (App.tsx:151-155). Reproduced: select type Talos, then vault Work -> list shows 1 item, heading still says 'Talos', two sidebar entries are highlighted simultaneously, Work's other 7 items are invisible, and there is no affordance to clear either filter.

Counts also collide: 'Passwords 3' (type count) and 'Personal 3' (vault total) render identically but mean different things.

Work:
- Dissolve the type dropdown into a flat, always-visible sidebar list; keep Views above and Vaults below.
- Default to 'All items'.
- Show every active filter as a removable chip in the list header, plus a reset action.
- Derive heading and count from the actual filter combination ('Work', '1 of 8').
- Differentiate type counts from vault counts visually (glyph vs dot).
- Selecting a view (Settings/Support/Generator) must clear the sidebar's selected appearance for item filters.
result:
The type dropdown is gone. Item types live in an always-visible icon rail (src/renderer/src/features/Rail.tsx) with counts in the tooltip; vaults moved to a title-bar context switcher with 'All vaults' as a first-class choice. Default filter is now 'All items'.

Active filters render as removable chips in the list header with a 'Clear all' action, the heading follows the narrowest active filter, and the count reads 'N of M' when a vault filter hides items. Selecting a panel (settings, support, generator) no longer leaves a type looking selected at the same time.

Covered by an e2e case asserting one chip becomes two and that 'Clear all' restores the full list.

name: Second UX review round: symmetry, selects, upsert editor, large-type window
description:
Second review round from the user's own screenshots, 2026-07-25. All fixed and measured.

Layout symmetry
- The detail reading column is centred in its pane instead of hugging the left edge. Measured left gap = right gap at every window size.
- Every modal is pixel-centred: measured dx=0 dy=0 for the type picker, the wide password editor, the default editor, the small create-vault modal, the shortcuts sheet and the sharing sheet, at 1440x900, 1100x760 and 900x620, including when the content overflows and the panel is capped. The command palette stays deliberately top-anchored at 12vh, which is the convention for that surface.
- Modal footers have a real gap between Cancel and the primary action. The old add-item footer used space-between with no gap between the sibling buttons; measured 8px everywhere now.
- The item-type trigger with its description crammed next to the title field is gone entirely, replaced by the type picker step.

Native selects
Every <select> is gone. ui/Fields.tsx now ships a Popover-based listbox: role=combobox trigger, portalled role=listbox, arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, Escape, and a check mark on the selected row. A real <select> cannot be styled past the trigger because macOS draws the popup itself, which is why the vault picker looked like a stock system menu.

Generator popover stability
Fixed width for both the standalone and inline forms, the options area reserves the height of the tallest mode, the generated value scrolls inside two fixed lines instead of growing, and the strength line is reserved rather than removed for PIN. Measured: identical x, y, width and height across Random, Memorable and PIN. An e2e assertion now guards this with an exact toEqual on the bounding box.

One upsert editor
components/AddItemModal.tsx and components/PassEditorModal.tsx are deleted. Creating starts with a small "What do you want to add?" picker, then opens features/ItemEditor.tsx, which is the same editor used for editing. Password items get the full field tree from features/PassFieldTree.tsx with arbitrary fields and sections nested up to four deep. Secrets, servers, SSH keys and the two config imports render their own shape in the same shell, because their payloads are fixed by the bridge contract and cannot take arbitrary fields.

Editor styling
The grey unstyled controls were literally unstyled: the field editor used bare <input> and <textarea> with no class, so the browser default rendered on a dark surface. Everything is on the primitives now.

Compact rows
Was a few pixels of row height. Now a real density change: the subtitle folds onto the title line, the avatar shrinks, and the row loses its vertical padding.

Large type
Now its own frameless always-on-top OS window at floating level, visible on all workspaces, that keeps the visible 30 second countdown and closes on Escape, on lock and on quit. It reuses the same preload, sandbox, contextIsolation and custom protocol as the main window, and gets its OWN stricter IPC sender check so it can reach only its four channels. The value travels renderer to main to window in memory, never through the URL, web storage, disk or the network. Falls back to the in-window modal if the window cannot be created.

Dead code
17 CSS classes that no component referenced any more were removed with their rule blocks, including the whole button-alias layer.

Verification: typecheck clean, 33 unit tests, 4 e2e tests (up from 3, with new guards for popover clipping, overlay Escape ordering, the custom listboxes, generator stability, filter chips and first run), bun run package succeeds. Isolated throwaway homes only; production ~/.fd0 and its agent were never touched. Nothing committed.

name: Create versioned desktop bridge API
description:
Part of fd0 desktop GUI. Add a high-level local application API without expanding fd0-agent into a vault/domain server.

Approach:
- Introduce a versioned request/response protocol over framed stdio, implemented by an internal fd0 subcommand or a small bundled Go bridge.
- Extract only the reusable domain operations needed by desktop from internal/cli so terminal I/O stays in CLI adapters.
- Bridge operations cover status, unlock, lock, pass list/search/get/create/update/remove, copy, TOTP, file import/export, scopes, sync, and progress/errors.
- Send credentials and secret values in message bodies, never argv or environment variables.
- Keep existing fd0-agent CBOR socket protocol and crypto responsibilities unchanged.
- Define cancellation, structured user-facing errors, capability/version handshake, and a hard frame limit.

Done when:
- The bridge has contract tests and malformed-input tests.
- A test client can complete unlock, pass CRUD, copy/TOTP, and sync against a temporary FD0_HOME.
- Secrets do not appear in process arguments or logs.
- Existing CLI behavior and Go tests remain green.
result: Implemented protocol v1 as a strict JSON-lines Go stdio bridge with 1 MiB frames, explicit capabilities and method allowlists, structured errors, secret wiping, malformed-input tests, inventory/detail/CRUD/auth/recovery/file operations, and a TypeScript supervisor that restarts crashed bridge processes without replaying failed writes.

name: Fix platform-local macOS manual smoke
description: Bug report from manual macOS platform-local testing: tests/manual_platform_macos.sh fails after unlock with auth method '*' not found because auth ls marks the active method with a leading '*'. A later run timed out during platform-local unlock because agent/client deadlines are 15s while LocalAuthentication/Keychain prompts can take longer. macOS also prompts for the login keychain password because fd0 CLI creates the Keychain item but fd0-agent later reads it, so macOS treats it as a different binary accessing confidential item. Fix by parsing auth ls robustly, extending platform-local unlock RPC deadlines, and moving platform-local provider enrollment into fd0-agent so the same binary creates and reads provider-local material. Verify dev-local integration, macOS store/delete smoke, targeted tests, and full go test where feasible.
result: Fixed the macOS platform-local manual smoke failures. Root causes: auth ls marks the active method with '*', so the scripts parsed '*' as method_id; platform-local unlock used the generic 15s RPC deadline, too short for OS prompts; macOS Keychain item was created by fd0 CLI and later read by fd0-agent, causing macOS to prompt for login keychain access for a different binary. Fixes: scripts now extract the first am_* token; platform-local unlock/enroll/remove RPCs get a 2m deadline on client and server; platform-local provider enrollment/removal moved into fd0-agent through new PlatformLocalAdd/Rm RPCs, so fd0-agent creates and reads its own Keychain item; macOS LocalAuthentication now requires biometrics instead of password fallback. Verification: go test ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/platformauth ./cmd/fd0 ./cmd/fd0-agent; bash tests/integration_platform_local.sh; macOS Keychain store/delete smoke; Linux cross-compile for platformauth/fd0/fd0-agent; manual script skips without opt-in; go run ./tools/threat-coverage; git diff --check; go test ./... all passed.

name: Add the private Desktop SFTP session bridge
description:
Expose the shared Go SFTP transport to Electron through a dedicated machine protocol without parsing public CLI output or moving file bytes through the renderer.

Design:
- Add a hidden helper mode to the bundled fd0 executable or an equivalently small packaged helper only if the existing binary cannot provide a clean lifecycle boundary.
- Use bounded framed messages for session start, directory listing, stat, upload, download, mkdir, rename, remove, progress, completion, cancellation, and close.
- Keep one SFTP connection per Files window and one transfer queue per connection. Terminal and Files sessions remain independent.
- Desktop main binds the helper to the selected immutable host reference and scope, owns native open/save dialogs and local filesystem paths, and sends only typed DTOs through preload.
- The renderer receives remote metadata, display-safe names, progress, and domain errors; it never receives arbitrary executable control, raw helper stdout, or file contents.
- Closing a Files window cancels active operations, closes the helper, and cannot destroy unrelated terminal or main-window state.

Security and lifecycle:
- Validate all IPC senders and message shapes with the existing hardened preload pattern.
- Limit concurrent operations and message sizes; reject stale session identifiers and duplicate completions.
- Keep local paths out of diagnostics and renderer state beyond user-facing basenames.
- Preserve native save/open permission behavior and safe local file modes.

Verification:
- Unit-test helper framing, malformed messages, progress ordering, cancellation races, destroyed windows, reconnect, and child cleanup.
- Unit-test IPC sender validation and ensure no arbitrary command or path primitive crosses the renderer boundary.
- Extend packaged-runtime checks so the helper path and native dependencies work in signed macOS and Linux bundles.
result: Implemented private NDJSON fd0-sftp-bridge with bounded frames, typed public errors, progress and cancellation, plus Electron helper client, packaged binary wiring, trusted-sender IPC, native file dialogs, and bridge protocol tests.
