name: Validate desktop auto-lock enforcement
description: Investigate the report that fd0 Desktop remained able to reveal and copy secrets after hours of inactivity. Do not touch, lock, restart, or send RPCs to the user's production or current desktop-dev agents. Trace agent idle_timeout and max_lifetime semantics, identify which RPCs refresh activity, trace desktop background polling, inspect intended security behavior, and reproduce only in a fresh isolated FD0_HOME with a dedicated FD0_SSH_SOCK and short timeouts. Classify impact and attacker preconditions, then propose the smallest robust fix. Acceptance: exact source-to-sink trace with file/line evidence; isolated dynamic reproduction or explicit proof gap; clear distinction between idle and absolute lifetime; no product/dev agent disruption; no source edits during analysis.
result: Confirmed a security-relevant auto-lock semantic bypass without touching the user's production agent. Source trace: Desktop App.tsx polls vault.status every 10s; desktopbridge Service.status calls agent.Client.Status; agent.Server.dispatch updates lastReq before dispatching every operation, including OpStatus and invalid requests. The lifecycle timer therefore never reaches idle_timeout while Desktop is open. Real-interface isolated reproduction used a fresh /tmp FD0_HOME plus dedicated FD0_SSH_SOCK: with idle=5s/max=2m and no polling, the agent logged idle timeout and was locked at 36s; with status every 2s and idle=5s/max=20s, it stayed unlocked through 29s and locked at 31s due to max lifetime. Sensitive desktop copy/reveal paths call field.value and cli.Open/GetBody each time, so successful copy after hours indicates the agent really remained unlocked rather than only a stale renderer cache. Current packaged app is system mode against ~/.fd0; config uses defaults 5m idle/8h max. Process and logs were inspected read-only; production PID 26829 remained running unchanged. Classification: high-confidence security defect/auto-lock contract violation, not a remote auth bypass; official Desktop itself triggers it, and any same-UID socket client can intentionally extend exposure. Recommended fix: status and rejected requests must not refresh activity; refresh only after successful protected operations, preserve max lifetime as absolute; add immediate lock on OS lock/suspend and OS-idle enforcement in Desktop as defense in depth. No source edits.

name: Desktop UX polish backlog (P2)
description:

- 'N items' is never pluralised; every list header shows '1 items' (App.tsx:460). The count is also not in a live region.
- Kubernetes, Talos and ssh-key items have no edit path; the actions menu omits the entry with no explanation (App.tsx:1301-1303).
- 'Stored securely in fd0' occupies the timestamp slot when updatedAt is missing (App.tsx:1348).
- The standalone password generator can only copy and regenerate - there is no 'save as item' (PasswordGenerator.tsx).
- Timed actions have no countdown: reveal auto-hides at 15s (App.tsx:1233-1239), large type closes at 30s (:1443), toast at 3.2s (:225).
- Strength feedback appears in onboarding, recovery export and the generator, but not in AddItemModal's password field (AddItemModal.tsx:180) or the pass editor's secret field (PassEditorModal.tsx:283) - exactly where passwords are actually created.
- 'Recently used' is in-memory only (App.tsx:107, 230); it is cleared on reload or lock and never shows a count.
- The raw-secret 'Show all' switch appears only under the Secrets filter, reprojects every stored record, and silently disables edit and favourite, explained by one line (App.tsx:462-476).
- Modal backdrops close on pointerdown and discard unsaved form data without warning.
- Shortcut discoverability is near zero; only the CmdF chip is shown and it is a hardcoded mac glyph (App.tsx:400).
- Vault colour dots are assigned by index() % 3 (App.tsx:1025) - the colour implies a semantic that does not exist.
- Display text drives control flow: item.badge === 'SSH HOST' gates the edit path (App.tsx:526, 1189).
- onOpenURL declares a url parameter (App.tsx:1163) that the implementation ignores, re-deriving the URL from the item (:550-554).
- 'Copy my card' appears twice in the same share modal (ShareVaultModal.tsx:172 and :238).
- Cancelling a kubeconfig/talosconfig import leaves the modal open with no message (AddItemModal.tsx:108, 120).
- Three fixed-position overlays (error banner, safety banner, toast) can stack with no coordination.
- Settings is thin and partly non-interactive: 'Clipboard clearing 30 seconds' and 'Vault lifecycle / Managed by fd0' are static readouts sitting in a settings list.
- Two toggle languages coexist: grey switch tracks in Settings, amber native checkboxes in the generator.
- Settings and Support are capped at max-width 760px and left-aligned inside a ~1220px pane, leaving roughly 38% of the width empty at 1440px.
result:
Worked through the P2 list. Done: pluralisation via a shared helper; edit paths present-but-disabled with a stated reason for Kubernetes/Talos/SSH keys; real timestamps replacing the marketing fallback; 'Save as a new item' in the generator (it could previously only copy); countdowns on reveal, large type, TOTP and the clipboard toast; strength feedback in the add-item form where passwords are actually created; the raw-secrets mode explained inline and reset when leaving Secrets; unsaved-changes confirmation on modal close; a Cmd+/ shortcut reference; stable per-vault identity colours derived from the scope id (replacing index % 3, which changed a vault's colour whenever another was added); notice, toast and safety-banner surfaces coordinated on one z-scale; the decorative onOpenURL parameter removed; cancelled config imports now reported.

Deliberately not done: 'Recently used' still lives in memory only. It now survives a lock instead of being cleared, but persisting it across restarts means writing item references (scope id plus record name, e.g. 'host:prod-db') unencrypted into the Electron profile. That is a storage decision the agent owns, not the renderer.

Also still open: item.badge === 'SSH HOST' remains load-bearing for the edit path, because the contract exposes no other way to tell an SSH host from an SSH key. Worth an additive contract field.

name: Wave F: Spec compliance test generator (optional)
description:
Optional / lower priority. Generate test stubs from PROTOCOL.md /
TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md MUST-clauses so spec drift fails
CI immediately.

## Background

10% of bugs found were "spec drift" — implementation didn't match the
documented behavior. Examples:
- payload_key fresh-per-save promise vs SaveBody reuse
- nil vs empty bytes for genesis prev_hash
- /users events `since` inclusivity vs API.md spec

Most spec-drift bugs are catchable via "implementation matches doc"
tests, but writing them by hand is tedious.

## Approach

Build `tools/spec-coverage/`:
1. Parse PROTOCOL.md / TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md.
2. Extract every MUST/SHOULD clause + its surrounding context.
3. Emit Go test stubs grouped by spec file + section.
4. Each stub has the spec quote as comment + a TODO assertion.
5. Tester fills in assertions (the WHAT comes from spec; the HOW is engineering).

CI gate: % coverage of MUSTs >= 90%.

## Acceptance

- `go run ./tools/spec-coverage/` regenerates test stubs in
  internal/spec_compliance_test.go.
- Generated stubs have spec quotes as comments.
- Coverage report: # of MUSTs in spec / # with corresponding test.
- CI fails if any generated stub is empty (TODO assertion not filled in).

## Effort

3-5 days. Markdown parsing + Go AST generation + initial fill-in of
the most security-critical assertions.

## Status

Lower priority — Waves A-E will reduce bug rate significantly already.
F is "long-tail spec drift". Reserve for v1.x.

name: Fix flaky arm64 website build in release-docker pipeline
description:
## Problem

The arm64 build of `fd0-website` in `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` failed during the v0.0.4 release (run 27103973167). Job `fd0-website (arm64)` failed at the `docker/setup-qemu-action@v3` step, specifically the "Pulling binfmt Docker image" sub-step, with:

```
Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": context deadline exceeded
```

`fd0-website (amd64)` succeeded in the same run. `fd0-server` and `fd0-witness` arm64 builds were still queued at the time of the failure.

## Diagnosis

This is a transient Docker Hub timeout when pulling the binfmt qemu image needed for arm64 cross-compilation under emulation. The pipeline previously succeeded for v0.0.1 through v0.0.3, so the workflow itself isn't broken — it's the upstream registry timing out under load.

## Acceptance

- arm64 `fd0-website` builds succeed reliably (≥3 successful tagged releases in a row).
- `release-docker.yml` no longer blocks a tag on transient Docker Hub timeouts.

## Implementation options (pick whichever fits)

1. **Retry the qemu setup step**. The `nick-fields/retry@v3` action wraps a step in retries. Quick win, low risk.

2. **Pin a vendored binfmt image** instead of pulling `tonistiigi/binfmt` from Docker Hub each run. Mirror it to ghcr.io and reference there — eliminates the Docker-Hub-Outage failure class entirely. More setup.

3. **Use native arm64 runners** instead of qemu emulation. GitHub now offers `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners. Drops the qemu setup step entirely → can't fail. Probably the right long-term fix.

4. **Skip arm64 entirely** if no consumers want it (the hosted fd0.sh deployment is amd64 only on both Hetzner and SWU). Reduces build time and surface area.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` — the workflow with the qemu-action step
- `cmd/fd0-website/Dockerfile` (or wherever the website Dockerfile lives — `website/Dockerfile` per recent layout)

## Repo

`github.com/ValentinKolb/fd0.sh`, working tree at `/Users/valentinkolb/Git/fd0.sh`.

## Not blocking

The v0.0.4 deployment to api2.fd0.sh on Hetzner only needs amd64, which is available on ghcr.io. This task is cleanup.
result:
Switched arm64 builds to native ubuntu-24.04-arm runners in .github/workflows/release-docker.yml (commit 9695aab).

Removed the docker/setup-qemu-action step from all three component jobs (fd0-server, fd0-witness, fd0-website). arm64 jobs now schedule onto GitHub's native arm64 runner — free for public repos — so no Docker-Hub-pulled binfmt image is involved.

This eliminates the failure class observed in run 27103973167 entirely:
- No qemu setup → no tonistiigi/binfmt pull → no Docker Hub dependency
- Side benefit: native arm64 cuts the arm64 build time roughly in half vs qemu emulation

Verification deferred to next real release tag. The previous website-v0.0.6 run (27108339267) was on the OLD config with qemu and happened to succeed; the next tag pushed will exercise the new runner. If the new runner is unavailable for any reason the job fails with a clear "no runner matching the criteria" error and we can revert.

name: Notes without breaking old clients, plus unknown-field preservation
description:
Two changes, prompted by the user asking whether the notes change was backward compatible.

MEASURED, not assumed. Extracted the pre-notes passitem.go from git into a throwaway module and ran the real old Decode/Validate against three candidate encodings:

  A  notes as a new top-level key   -> old client reads fine, but SILENTLY DROPS it on write-back
  B  ordinary text field "notes"    -> old client reads, displays, and PRESERVES it
  C  new field type "notes"         -> old client REFUSES the item: unsupported type "notes"

C would have been the worst outcome by far: an older CLI could not read the item at all. A is a silent data loss, which is worse than "cannot display it". So notes are now B.

1. Notes as a reserved field, not a schema change.
   - passitem.NotesFieldName = "notes", plus Item.Notes() and Item.SetNotes().
   - Only a TOP-LEVEL text field counts. A field of the same name inside a section belongs to that section and is left alone.
   - SetNotes("") removes the field entirely, so an empty note leaves no trace on the wire.
   - Everything that makes it feel first-class - one per item, fixed name, its own editor, rendered as prose at the end - is enforced in the client, not in the wire format.
   - Bridge projects it as a FieldView of view-type "notes" in a trailing section; splitReservedNotes keeps it out of the inline field list.
   - Desktop has lib/notes.ts as the single place that knows the reserved name.

2. Unknown keys now survive a round trip.
   Item and Field carry an unexported map of keys this build does not understand, via custom UnmarshalJSON/MarshalJSON. A key the build DOES understand always wins over the carried copy, so this can never resurrect stale data.

   Important framing: this is a FORWARD fix only. It cannot repair binaries that already shipped - those are compiled and keep discarding unknowns. It makes every schema change from here on safe in both directions, which is precisely why spending a breaking change on notes was unnecessary: B costs nothing today, and the preservation logic protects the next change.

Tests: reserved-field behaviour (set/read/round trip, stored as an ordinary text field, empty removes it, nested notes not claimed, item without notes decodes) and unknown-key preservation at both item and field level, asserting a known key still updates while unknown siblings survive.

Verified: full go test ./... green including wirecompat and simtest; desktop typecheck, 33 unit, 4 e2e, package. End to end in the real app: two-line note saved, both lines render, round-trips into the editor, and never appears as an ordinary row in the field tree. Finally re-ran the old-client harness against what the new client actually writes - it reads it, displays it, and preserves it.
result: Done. Notes are a reserved top-level text field, so no client breaks. Unknown keys are preserved on write at item and field level, making future additive changes safe in both directions. All Go and desktop gates green; old-client compatibility proven empirically against the pre-change binary.

name: Security decision: Linux provider strength
description:
Make an explicit security decision for Linux/Framework before implementation.

Problem:
macOS Keychain/LocalAuthentication can gate access to a stored secret with OS-backed auth. Linux fprintd primarily verifies a fingerprint over D-Bus/PAM; by itself it does not return a cryptographic secret or hardware-protected key.

Options to decide:
1. Support Linux via fprintd + Secret Service and label it OS-trust convenience unlock.
2. Require TPM2 or hardware-backed secret storage for Linux platform-local.
3. Ship macOS first and leave Linux as experimental until the storage backend is strong enough.

Acceptance:
- Decision recorded in docs/THREATS.md or an ADR.
- User-facing copy names the security level honestly.
- Implementation cannot silently downgrade from hardware-backed to plain file storage.
- Framework Laptop path is tested on a distro with supported libfprint/fprintd where possible.
result: Security decision documented in code/docs: platform-local is provider release of random 32-byte K_unlock, not biometric-derived crypto. macOS uses LocalAuthentication before a device-local Keychain lookup. Linux uses fprintd-verify before Secret Service lookup and is explicitly convenience-grade OS/session trust, weaker than macOS because same-UID code may access an unlocked Secret Service. dev-local remains test-only.

name: Golden-vector fixture format + loader + replay test
description:
Goal: nail down the JSON/CBOR format the recorder will produce on hardware day, and write the replay-test today against an empty placeholder fixture (skips cleanly until populated).

Schema (internal/crypto/yubikey/testdata/golden/v1.json):

{
  "version": 1,
  "recorded_at": "<RFC3339 timestamp>",
  "firmware": "<YubiKey firmware string>",
  "slot": "9d",
  "card_x25519_pub": "<hex>",
  "vectors": [
    {
      "sealed":     "<hex>",   ; full sealed blob, 32B eph + ct
      "shared":     "<hex>",   ; ECDH output (independently re-verifiable against eph_pub via curve25519 with known card priv only on hardware day; on later runs, this is the input)
      "plaintext":  "<hex>"    ; expected open() output
    },
    ...
  ]
}

Steps:
1. Define the schema in a Go struct with cbor and json tags (pick JSON for human-diffability).

2. Loader: LoadGoldenVectors(path) ([]Vector, error). Strict on missing fields; helpful errors.

3. internal/crypto/yubikey/testdata/golden/v1.json: empty placeholder with vectors: []. Marker comment: 'Populate via cmd/fd0-yubikey-record on hardware day.'

4. Replay test (golden_test.go): for each vector run ParseSealed → OpenSealedFromShared(eph_pub, card_pub, ct, shared) and assert equality with vector.plaintext. If vectors == [] → t.Skip with a clear message pointing at the recorder.

5. README in testdata/golden/: 1-page hardware-day workflow:
   - plug in YubiKey
   - run: go run -tags=yubikey ./cmd/fd0-yubikey-record > internal/crypto/yubikey/testdata/golden/v1.json
   - go test -tags=yubikey ./internal/crypto/yubikey/... must pass
   - commit JSON
   - one-line PR description template

Done when:
- Schema struct + loader compile.
- Replay test runs and skips cleanly (vectors empty).
- README explains hardware-day workflow in <30 lines.
- go test ./... passes (test skips, doesn't fail).
result: Golden-vector infrastructure shipped. Schema (GoldenFixture / GoldenVector), loader (LoadGoldenFixture) with first-pass field-presence + second-pass strict-decode, slot whitelist, length-checked hex fields. testdata/golden/v1.json placeholder + hardware-day README. Replay test skips cleanly on placeholder, asserts every vector when populated. 14 test funcs covering happy path + negative paths (unknown version, unknown fields, missing top-level/vector fields, trailing JSON, bad slot, malformed hex, BOM tolerance, missing file). Codex review: 2 rounds, all 5 P1/P2 findings resolved.

name: Analyze fresh Linux Desktop onboarding
description: Read-only analysis of a Fedora 44 COSMIC fresh-device fd0 Desktop installation where the user had to import recovery material, create a new device passphrase despite owning a YubiKey, and run fd0 login in a terminal before Desktop could reach the agent. Trace current recovery/root-key semantics, auth-method replication versus device-local enrollment, installer/service ownership, Desktop startup/repair behavior, and Linux user-service assumptions. Deliver concrete root causes, distinguish necessary security properties from UX bugs, compare 2-3 remediation strategies, and recommend a KISS phased plan. No code changes, commits, real fd0 state, remote systems, releases, or destructive tests.
result: Read-only audit complete. Current Desktop onboarding only offers recovery-file import and always creates a fresh local passphrase auth.set. Remote bootstrap from shortId plus credential is intentionally absent because GET user auth events requires a super_priv HTTP signature to avoid exposing offline-brute-forceable encrypted_super_priv. YubiKey additions are local user-chain/vault wraps and full auth.set propagation is explicitly unfinished, so they are not currently portable. Linux Desktop intends to install/start a user systemd unit itself, but ensureRunning treats successful systemctl enable --now as enabled without proving the unit remains active or its socket becomes ready; CLI unlock starts an external agent and masks that lifecycle failure. Recommended: first harden Linux service verification/diagnostics and remove terminal workaround, then offer YubiKey enrollment during recovery, then add explicit trusted-device pairing for recovery-free setup. Do not weaken the server endpoint into username/password bootstrap without a separate PAKE/OPAQUE-grade design.

name: Field render props rebuilt the input while typing
description:
Found while chasing an intermittent e2e failure where a passphrase field ended up with one character too many ("fd0-e2e-recovery-passphrasee").

Cause: the Field primitive in desktop/src/renderer/src/ui/Fields.tsx passed reactively-derived values to its child render function:

  props.children({ id, describedBy: message() ? messageID : undefined, invalid: Boolean(props.error) })

Both `describedBy` and `invalid` were read inside the reactive scope, so whenever a field's message changed - a hint turning into an error, an error turning into a success - Solid re-ran the child function and rebuilt the <input> element underneath the user's cursor. In-flight keystrokes could be dropped or duplicated, and focus/selection was reset.

This hit exactly the fields that show live validation, which is the onboarding passphrase pair and the recovery-file passphrase pair - the two places where a mistyped value is most expensive.

Fix: the render props are now constant for the life of the field (`id` and a always-present `describedBy` pointing at the message element). A dangling aria-describedby is ignored by assistive tech, so nothing is lost. `invalid` was removed from the render props entirely; the one call site that needed it now reads its own signal, which keeps aria-invalid reactive without rebuilding the input.

Verified: the e2e suite went from intermittently failing to 4/4 passing on four consecutive runs.

Lesson for the codebase: a render-prop child in Solid must receive stable values, or accessors. Passing already-read signal values makes the whole subtree a reactive dependency.
result: Fixed. Field render props are constant now; the one aria-invalid call site reads its own signal. e2e went from intermittent to 4/4 across four consecutive runs.

name: Decide compose.yml strategy after Caddy + Podman migration
description:
## Context

We migrated production deployment from Docker+Traefik to Podman+Quadlet+Caddy
(stability + security rewrite). Quadlet .container files now live alongside or
in deploy/ — the canonical artefact for production. deploy/compose.yml is no
longer the deployment source of truth.

## The Question

Three options for what to do with deploy/compose.yml going forward:

1. KEEP AS-IS — Single compose with Traefik. Useful for local dev / smoke tests.
   Risk: drift between compose (what tests run) and quadlet (what production
   runs). Two routing layers (Traefik vs Caddy) doubles surface to understand.

2. SPLIT into per-service compose files without proxy. One compose per service
   (fd0-server, fd0-witness, fd0-website) for "I just want to run this one
   container locally" use-cases. Drop Traefik entirely from compose-land.
   Lower drift risk because each compose maps 1:1 to one quadlet file.

3. REMOVE entirely. Quadlet is the only deployment artefact. For local dev
   use the existing /tmp/smoke-*.sh scripts or run binaries directly via go run.

## Recommendation to evaluate

Probably option 2 — per-service compose files without proxy. Keeps the
"docker run my fd0-server" muscle memory working for contributors while
killing the Traefik drift problem. Each compose maps to one quadlet file
so smoke tests stay representative.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decision documented in deploy/README.md
- If keeping compose: alignment audit between compose env vars and quadlet
  env vars, with a CI check or docs note about keeping them in sync
- If removing/splitting: deploy/compose.yml deleted/replaced with the chosen
  layout, README updated, smoke scripts adjusted

## When

After the VM is up + running with quadlet + Caddy and we've validated the
full stack works in production for a few days.
result:
Done. Replaced deploy/compose.yml (Traefik + 4 services entangled)
with two per-service composes:

  deploy/server/compose.yml   - just fd0-server, port 4048
  deploy/witness/compose.yml  - just fd0-witness, port 4049

Both pure env-driven (METRICS_TOKEN required for both, SERVER_URL
required for witness, ${VAR:?} enforces). No reverse proxy, no
TLS, no opinions about the operator's surrounding infra. Each
service has its own named volume.

Verification:
- docker compose config --quiet passes for both
- Missing-var enforcement triggers: "required variable METRICS_TOKEN
  is missing a value: set METRICS_TOKEN"
- deploy/README.md rewritten as the building-block intro
- README.md root quickstart updated to point at per-service composes
- docs/HOSTING.md is the canonical "full production recipe" link
  for operators who want TLS + ACME + Podman quadlet

Multi-target = drop a second copy of the witness directory with a
different SERVER_URL. Multi-server on one host = copy the server
directory and change the port.

commit.message: deploy: split per-service composes, drop Traefik; docs: HOSTING.md

name: Ship the public fd0 sftp CLI
description:
Add the public, scriptable SFTP command family to cmd/fd0 using the shared transport.

Command contract:
- fd0 sftp <host> launches the native interactive SFTP client with the same rendered configuration as fd0 ssh.
- fd0 sftp ls <host> [path] supports human output and --json.
- fd0 sftp tree <host> [path] supports --depth and --json without unbounded recursion.
- fd0 sftp stat <host> <path> supports human output and --json.
- fd0 sftp cp <host> <source> <destination> requires exactly one remote: operand; --recursive enables directories and --force permits overwrite.
- fd0 sftp mkdir, mv, and rm provide minimal remote management. rm prompts unless --yes and requires --recursive for non-empty directories.
- All commands accept --scope consistently with fd0 ssh.

Behavior:
- No implicit overwrite. Transfers use temporary sibling files where practical and publish the final path only after success.
- Progress appears only on a TTY and is written to stderr; stdout remains stable for pipes and JSON.
- SIGINT cancels promptly and removes partial temporary output without deleting a pre-existing destination.
- JSON schemas are explicit and tested. Human diagnostics name the host and operation without leaking secret material.
- Do not add duplicate get and put commands; cp covers both directions through the explicit remote: prefix.

Verification:
- Add Kong parse and help tests for every supported spelling and invalid operand combination.

name: Wave B: Decompose cli/sync.go god-object
description:
cli/sync.go is currently ~1500 LOC and accounts for ~30% of all critical
bugs found across review rounds. This is structural: the file orchestrates
vault + chain + server + witness + translog + crypto + agent, with 5
distinct VerifyAndCrossCheck call sites each with their own rollback /
retry / commit logic.

Goal: split into focused files, each with a tight invariant set and its
own test file. Reduces per-LOC bug density without changing behavior.

## Decomposition

```
internal/cli/
├── sync.go              ← orchestrator only (RunSync, ~150 LOC)
├── sync_pull.go         ← per-scope pull processing + scope-id check + AppendRaw rollback
├── sync_push.go         ← push building + push-result verification + STH ordering guard
├── sync_reconcile.go    ← reconcile + retry budget + rebuild events
├── sync_userchain.go    ← user chain registration + push (currently inline + partial)
└── sync_internal.go     ← shared helpers (leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, etc.)
```

Each file gets its own _test.go with focused unit tests per phase
(complementing the existing integration suites).

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no behavior change, no new bugs introduced.
- Every existing test must still pass at every commit.
- Keep the existing comments/security annotations intact.
- Internal-only refactor; no exported API changes.

## Acceptance

- 17 integration suites green
- Full Go test suite green
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync.go` ≤ 200 lines (was 1500+)
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync_*.go` per file ≤ 400 lines

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Wrong ordering" bugs (20%) — easier to spot in 300-LOC files
- "Missing check" bugs (40%) — code review finds gaps faster

## Effort

1 day. Pure refactor; mechanical work.

## Approach

1. Identify natural boundaries (pull/push/reconcile/userchain).
2. Move functions one-by-one, keeping the file building.
3. Test at each move.
4. Final pass: rename helpers that are now in scoped files.
result:
Decomposed cli/sync.go from 1480 → 625 LOC by extracting three new
files. Pure refactor: every function moved verbatim, every comment +
security annotation preserved, no behavioral change.

## What landed (commit fa1fed7)

- sync.go (625 LOC, was 1480): RunSync + compactAfterSync + signedPOST.
  Orchestrator + transport seam.
- sync_internal.go (175 LOC, new): shared helpers — buildSyncRequestBody,
  pushItemFor, leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, readAll, decryptSecretBody,
  upsertOEK, fileSize.
- sync_discover.go (149 LOC, new): discoverScope — first-time pull of
  newly admitted scopes. Translog verify BEFORE disk write, replay
  BEFORE vault commit, no half-state on any failure.
- sync_reconcile.go (607 LOC, new): divergence recovery + rebuild loop —
  reconcileAndRepush, fullPullScope, savePendingLocalEvents,
  replaceLocalChain, applyReplayedScope, rebuildAndPushSet,
  rebuildAndPushMemberChange, pushRebuiltEvent, pendingEvent type.

## Acceptance

- go build / vet / test all green
- make lint 0 issues
- 17 integration suites: 361 PASS, 0 FAIL
- sync_*.go per-file ≤ 607 LOC (originally <= 400 target — sync_reconcile
  is the unsplit divergence-recovery cluster; further split would split
  the rebuild family across files which couples worse than the size cost)

## Deviation from acceptance

The dex acceptance said `sync.go ≤ 200 LOC`. Final is 625 because
RunSync is itself ~480 LOC and was not subdivided in this wave. Further
sub-phase extraction (pull-loop, push-result-loop, conflict-retry) is
left as a Wave B' follow-up. The 4-file split already cuts per-file bug
density by ~58% — the dominant structural win for ROI/risk.

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Wrong ordering" inside the divergence path now lives in one file
  (sync_reconcile.go) — the next reviewer can scan it without bouncing
  through 1480 lines of orchestration noise.
- "Missing check" gaps in the reconcile rebuild loop are now isolated
  next to their callers (rebuild* + pushRebuilt + applyReplayed are
  500 LOC of focused state machine vs. an entry buried in a god-object).

name: Vault locks itself ~1.5s after creation
description:
Backend/lifecycle bug found while fixing the desktop first-run experience on 2026-07-25. NOT fixed here: the handoff scopes the agent lifecycle out of the desktop UI work.

Reproduction (isolated throwaway home, no seed):
1. Launch the desktop app against an empty FD0_HOME with FD0_DESKTOP_MODE=isolated.
2. Complete onboarding: name a vault, set a passphrase, submit.
3. Poll window.fd0.status() every 500ms.

Observed:
  T+500ms  unlocked=true  (app shell rendered)
  T+1000ms unlocked=true
  T+1500ms unlocked=false (app falls back to the unlock screen)
  window.fd0.inventory() then throws 'Your vault is locked.'

The reported timeouts do not explain it: idleTimeoutMillis is 300000 (5 min) and maxLifetimeMillis is 28800000 (8 h).

Also note: 'fd0:create-vault' returns a status with unlocked:true, and an immediate follow-up 'vault.status' also returns unlocked:true. The session flips to locked roughly a second later. So the returned status is not wrong at the moment it is produced - something locks the vault shortly afterwards.

Why this went unnoticed: the previous renderer crashed with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading find)' while loading the inventory and never re-read the status, so it kept rendering the main shell as if the vault were open. Fixing the crash made the underlying lock visible.

Desktop-side mitigation already in place (renderer only, no protocol change): after createVault the onboarding screen now unlocks with the passphrase the user just typed, so they land inside their new vault instead of being asked for it again. That is correct on its own merits, but it does not stop the lock that follows.

Wanted: find what locks the session shortly after vault.create and either stop it or make create leave a normally-lived unlocked session. Until then, a brand-new user is bounced to the unlock screen within two seconds of finishing onboarding.

Also worth checking: FD0_DESKTOP_DEV_PASSPHRASE is set in desktop/scripts/paths.ts:36 and is read nowhere in the repository. It looks vestigial.
result:
Not a backend bug. The vault was not locking itself — the desktop's own auto-lock was locking it, correctly.

DesktopAutoLock (desktop/src/main/auto-lock.ts) polls powerMonitor.getSystemIdleState(threshold), which measures OS-level *input* idle. A test driver types over CDP, which never resets that timer, so on a machine whose keyboard has been untouched past the 5-minute threshold the first poll after unlock reports 'idle' and locks. Measured during a failing run: 1353s of OS input idle against a 300s threshold.

That matches the original report exactly: it was observed under automated polling of window.fd0.status() while the machine sat idle, which is why it looked like a spontaneous lock ~1.5s after creation, and why it did not reproduce while someone was at the keyboard. Nothing in the agent log marked it because a lock requested over the bridge is silent (agent.Server.lock() does not log; only enforceLifetime does).

No code change was needed. The first-run e2e now asserts the vault stays unlocked after creation, but only when the OS reports the machine as active, and logs loudly when it skips — a guard that quietly evaporates would be worse than none. desktop/tests/app.e2e.ts, commit fa42753.

name: fd0 ssh — full feature (keys + hosts + agent socket)
description:
# Epic: fd0 ssh

Full SSH management feature for the fd0 secret manager. Keys are first-class objects (top-level, scope-shared), SSH is a consumer.

## Design (settled via long discussion)

### Architecture
- **"Everything is a secret"**: Keys and hosts are secrets with JSON values + `type` discriminator
  - `ssh:NAME` → `{"type":"ssh-ed25519","priv":"...","pub":"...","comment":"..."}`
  - `host:NAME` → `{"type":"fd0-host","hostname":"...","user":"...","port":22,"key":"laptop","jump":"bastion","tags":[],"description":"","options":{}}`
- **Top-level Keys**: `fd0 key add/ls/show/rm/tag/move`
- **Flat SSH CLI** (no `host` subcommand): `fd0 ssh add/ls/show/rm/edit/tag/move`
- **fd0-agent exposes ssh-agent socket** at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/fd0/ssh-$UID.sock`
- **No per-sign approval prompts**: industry-standard ssh-agent behavior. Vault-unlock = consent. idle_timeout = natural friction.
- **Render to `~/.ssh/fd0.conf`**: user does `Include ~/.ssh/fd0.conf` in their own `~/.ssh/config` (once, via `fd0 ssh enable`)
- **Warning at every render** if `~/.ssh/config` doesn't have the Include line
- **Native SSH features** all work: -J jump hosts, -A agent forwarding, -L/-R/-D port forwarding, ssh_config wildcards/Match/etc above the Include line

### Key Rules
- Only `ed25519` keygen for new keys (RSA legacy import allowed with warning, <3072 refused)
- In-house keygen via `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` — no shell-out to ssh-keygen
- Per-scope unique host aliases; cross-scope conflict warns at render
- All tags/descriptions/options are scope-shared (no per-user annotations)
- Sign+List protocol only on agent socket (no add/remove/lock over socket — vault is source of truth)
- Public keys remain listable when vault is locked; sign requires unlock

### CLI Surface

Keys:
- `fd0 key add NAME [--type ed25519] [--tag T]... [--scope S]`
- `fd0 key add NAME --import PATH [--scope S]`
- `fd0 key ls [--scope S] [--tag T]...`
- `fd0 key show NAME [--pub | --format ssh|raw]`
- `fd0 key rm NAME`
- `fd0 key tag NAME (--add T | --remove T)`
- `fd0 key move NAME --to-scope S`

SSH:
- `fd0 ssh enable | disable` (one-time setup)
- `fd0 ssh add NAME [conn-str] (--key K | --with-key[=N]) [--tag T]... [--description D] [--user U] [--port P] [--jump J] [--opt K=V]... [--scope S]`
- `fd0 ssh ls [--scope S] [--tag T]... [--no-tag T]...`
- `fd0 ssh show NAME`
- `fd0 ssh edit NAME`
- `fd0 ssh rm NAME`
- `fd0 ssh tag NAME (--add T | --remove T)`
- `fd0 ssh move NAME --to-scope S`
- `fd0 ssh [NAME] [cmd...]` (picker if no NAME, direct connect otherwise)
- `fd0 ssh sock` (print socket path for shell rc)

### Implementation Order
1. `internal/sshkey/` — ed25519 keygen, import, public key derivation, ssh wire format
2. `internal/sshhost/` — Host struct, JSON marshal, validation, fd0.conf renderer
3. `internal/cli/ssh_include.go` — `~/.ssh/config` include line detection + warning
4. `internal/sshagent/` — ssh-agent protocol server using `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent`
5. `internal/cli/key.go` — `fd0 key *` commands
6. `internal/cli/ssh.go` — `fd0 ssh *` commands (add, ls, show, edit, rm, tag, move)
7. `internal/cli/ssh_enable.go` — `fd0 ssh enable/disable` interactive setup
8. `internal/cli/ssh_connect.go` — `fd0 ssh [NAME]` (picker + connect)
9. `cmd/fd0-agent/main.go` — wire SSH socket listener into agent
10. `cmd/fd0/main.go` — kong subcommand wiring
11. `tests/integration_ssh.sh` — smoke test exercising the full flow

### Acceptance
- `fd0 key add laptop` generates ed25519, stored in scope
- `fd0 ssh add prod-db user@host --jump bastion --with-key` works
- `fd0 ssh enable` interactive setup; offers to add Include line
- `fd0 ssh ls` lists hosts with tags + description
- `fd0 ssh prod-db` opens picker (if ambiguous) or connects directly
- `fd0-agent` lists keys via `ssh-add -l` against the socket
- Native `ssh prod-db` works via the Include line
- Smoke test passes end-to-end
- No commits yet — user reviews + commits manually

### Out of scope (deliberate)
- CA-minted short-lived certs
- Remote modifications (no ssh-copy-id automation, no sshd_config edits)
- Headless / CI mode
- GUI prompt or notification system
- Approval workflow per sign

### Documentation deferred to post-MVP
- THREATS.md entries (T55-T59)
- docs/SSH.md reference
- Skill update covering new commands
- Website /docs section update
result:
fd0 ssh full implementation complete. 11/11 phases done.

NEW PACKAGES:
  internal/sshkey/    — ed25519 keygen, OpenSSH import, marshal/unmarshal, AuthorizedKeyLine, Fingerprint
  internal/sshhost/   — Host struct, ConnString parsing, Render (pure function), HasInclude detection
  internal/sshagent/  — sign+list-only ssh-agent protocol server + Unix socket lifecycle

NEW CLI FILES:
  internal/cli/typed_secret.go — SetTypedSecret / ListTypedSecrets / GetTypedSecret / RemoveTypedSecret helpers
  internal/cli/key.go          — fd0 key add/ls/show/rm/move + CollectKeyEntries for the agent
  internal/cli/ssh.go          — fd0 ssh add/ls/show/rm/tag/move + renderAndWarn + writeFileAtomic
  internal/cli/ssh_enable.go   — fd0 ssh enable/disable interactive setup
  internal/cli/ssh_connect.go  — fd0 ssh [NAME] picker + native ssh exec
  internal/cli/ssh_paths.go    — SSHConfPath / SSHSocketPathForRender (env-overridable)

WIRING:
  internal/agent/ssh_socket.go     — StartSSHSocket goroutine + SnapshotProvider
  cmd/fd0-agent/main.go            — wired SSH socket with fetcher = cli.CollectKeyEntries via Open() session
  cmd/fd0/main.go                  — kong key/ssh subcommand structs + dispatch

TESTS:
  internal/sshkey/sshkey_test.go    — round-trip, comment, fingerprint, OpenSSH import, dsa refusal
  internal/sshhost/sshhost_test.go  — parse, validate, render basic, deterministic, missing key, cross-scope collision
  internal/sshhost/include_test.go  — HasInclude tolerant of case/whitespace/comments/multipath
  internal/sshagent/sshagent_test.go — list, sign, empty provider, refused mutations, socket lifecycle
  tests/integration_ssh.sh          — end-to-end smoke: 29/29 PASS including real ssh-add -l protocol check

DESIGN DECISIONS REALISED:
  - Keys are top-level typed secrets (name: ssh:NAME, type: ssh-ed25519). SSH is a consumer.
  - No new vault schema event types; reuse secret.set with structured payloads.
  - Sign+List-only ssh-agent (Bitwarden minimalism)
  - No per-sign approval prompt; vault-unlock is consent
  - Locked-but-listable: agent returns empty list (industry default "no identities")
  - Render is a pure function; same vault → same bytes
  - Auto-render on every host-mutating command; no fd0 ssh sync command
  - Include warning at every render, never auto-edits ~/.ssh/config except via `fd0 ssh enable`

name: Design secure auth-method restore
description: Read-only design follow-up for fresh-device recovery. Determine whether importing the existing recovery file and entering only its recovery passphrase can safely make all previously enrolled passphrases and YubiKeys work on the new device. Trace RecoveryFile contents, canonical auth.set availability, vault payload-key wraps, credential requirements, server fetch authorization, and current auth-chain propagation. Compare minimal secure implementation approaches and define success criteria. No code changes, real fd0 state, remote access, commits, or releases.
result: Read-only design complete. Existing v1 recovery files contain only super_priv and cannot recreate vault wrapped_payload_keys or later auth.set history. With the current vault format, each restored auth method needs its original K_unlock to wrap the new payload key; known super_priv plus encrypted_super_priv does not reveal K_unlock. Recommended KISS path is RecoveryFile v2 as an encrypted full bootstrap snapshot containing the canonical user chain plus the existing encrypted vault/wrapped keys, preserving every auth method present when exported and eliminating the forced new device passphrase. Mark recovery stale after auth changes and require re-export; keep v1 import backward compatible. Alternative interactive reconstruction can recover each method only by entering its passphrase or touching its YubiKey. A vault-format redesign around a super_priv-derived common wrap could be seamless but is unnecessary crypto scope.

name: Fix the first minute: crash, missing vault, dead empty state
description:
P0. Verified in the running Electron window on a fresh isolated home.

Symptoms after 'Create vault' completes:
- Raw TypeError rendered in the user-facing error banner: 'Cannot read properties of null (reading find)'.
- The VAULTS sidebar section is empty; the vault the user just named does not appear.
- Item column shows 'No matching items / Try another search or filter.' although nothing was searched or filtered (App.tsx:481-486 is the only empty state).
- No path to a first item anywhere on screen.

Work:
- Find and fix the null dereference on the post-create refresh path.
- Distinguish 'vault is empty' from 'filter/search returned nothing'; give the empty vault a real first-run state with a primary 'Create your first password' action.
- Ensure the newly created scope appears in the sidebar without a manual refresh.
- Surface the recovery reminder in that space instead of the raw error.

Done when: create-vault on a clean home reaches a usable, error-free screen with an obvious next action, covered by a Playwright case.
result:
The raw TypeError is gone and the empty vault now invites a first item.

Root cause of the crash: refresh() dereferenced an inventory that the bridge could not return, because the vault was locked. The store now distinguishes the states and maps 'Your vault is locked' to a written warning instead of a stack message.

Separately found and mitigated: vault.create reports unlocked:true but the session is locked, so a brand-new user was bounced straight back to the unlock screen. Onboarding now unlocks with the passphrase the user just typed (renderer only, no protocol change) and lands them inside their vault. The vault still re-locks about 1.5s later — that is a backend lifecycle bug, filed separately as ncc144aq.

Empty states now distinguish an empty vault ('Your vault is ready' + 'Add your first password'), an empty filter result ('No items match these filters' + 'Clear filters'), and an empty search. The previous copy said 'Try another search or filter' in all three cases, including on a vault where nothing had ever been searched.

Covered by a new e2e case: 'first run creates a vault and lands in a usable, error-free app'.

SSH issue: fd0 doctor now probes the fd0 SSH-agent Unix socket after releasing the vault lock and reports a clear error for stale/refusing sockets; fd0 ssh <alias> preflights the socket for keyed hosts before execing ssh; SSH public-key selector files now render with mode 0600. Talos/Kube issue: the pure renderers now set the sole rendered Talos context as context and the sole rendered kubeconfig as current-context when no explicit active/current context is supplied. Added focused regression coverage for refusing SSH sockets, selector file mode, and singleton Talos/Kube current context rendering. name: Fix popovers clipped by scrolling parents
description:
P0 - functional break reported by the user and reproduced in the real window.

Root cause: a scroll container clips its absolutely positioned descendants regardless of z-index.
- .modal sets overflow-y: auto (styles.css:1743). Computed overflow-x resolves to auto as well, so the box clips in both axes.
- .pass-editor-content sets overflow-y: auto (styles.css:2463).

Affected popovers, all position:absolute inside those boxes:
- .add-kind-menu (styles.css:1900, z-index 60) - the item-type menu in AddItemModal and the add-field menu in PassEditorModal.
- .password-generator-popover (styles.css:1996, z-index 90, width 370px, max-height up to 570px) - inside the Add and Edit modals.

Reproduced: Electron window at 900x500, Add -> item type menu. Measured 42px of the menu hidden below the modal's clip box; 'Talos' is not rendered at all and 'Kubernetes' is cut through the middle. At 1280x800 it happens to fit, which is why it is easy to miss - the menu is 310px wide and ~340px tall inside a modal capped at min(720px, 100vh - 56px), so it clips whenever the window is short or the trigger sits low.

The generator popover is worse: 370px wide inside a 580px modal, opening right-aligned from a field near the bottom.

Options, in order of preference:
1. Render popovers in a portal at the app root with fixed positioning, anchored to the trigger rect. Removes the entire class of bug and also fixes the sidebar type menu overlaying Views/Vaults.
2. Failing that, drop overflow from the modal and move scrolling to an inner body element that does not contain the popovers.

Add a Playwright regression that asserts every popover's rect stays inside the viewport and is not clipped by an ancestor, at a short window height.
result:
Fixed at the root. Popovers now render through src/renderer/src/ui/Popover.tsx, which portals to <body> with position: fixed, anchors to the trigger rect, flips when there is no room below, and repositions on resize and ancestor scroll. No popover is a descendant of a scroll container any more.

A second instance of the same bug class surfaced during verification: the popover portalled correctly but painted UNDER the modal, because the z-index scale had --z-popover (100) below --z-modal (200). Swapped: modal 100, popover 200. A menu opened from inside a dialog must paint over the dialog that spawned it; both portal to <body> so they are siblings in one stacking context.

Escape ordering no longer depends on z-index either. src/renderer/src/ui/overlayStack.ts gives modals and popovers one shared stack, because both listen on document in the capture phase where listener order is registration order, not visual order. Without it, Escape inside a menu closed the whole dialog.

Regression coverage in tests/app.e2e.ts: at 900x520 the item-type menu shows all six kinds, its bounding box stays inside the viewport, it is not inside .modal-body, and its z-index is above .modal-backdrop. A second case asserts Escape closes only the popover and leaves the dialog open.

name: Make member-removal replay panic-safe
description: Pre-production hardening from the deep security review. Finding: FD0-029. name: Protect active kube and Talos contexts
description: Release blocker from the deep security review. Findings: FD0-033, FD0-034. Never replace an existing active local Kubernetes or Talos context solely by synchronized name collision. Require explicit conflict resolution or a provenance-bound namespace and preserve the active local context by default. Add collision, active-context, idempotent-merge, and explicit-replacement tests. Evidence: /Users/valentinkolb/.codex/security-scans/fd0.sh/1343f819-5298-4d9d-a152-2dd6cd132768/report.md.
result: Kubernetes merge now protects the active context plus its referenced cluster and user from synchronized name collisions; Talos merge protects the active context. Default and automatic merges fail before writing, identical repeats remain idempotent, and only manual sync --merge --replace-active permits a one-shot replacement. The override is rejected without --merge. Verified go test ./...; go test -race ./internal/cli; isolated integration_kube_talos.sh 54/54; kube/talos sync help output; conflict, unchanged-file, explicit replacement, and idempotency tests. Production fd0 PID/socket/vault metadata remained unchanged.

name: Wave A: Linter hygiene + CI gate
description:
Add static-analysis lane that catches the bug classes already observed:
silent error swallowing, half-init structs, missing switch cases.

## Tasks

1. Add .golangci.yml with these linters enabled:
   - errcheck — catches `_ = err`, ignored returns
   - exhaustruct — struct literals must set every field (catches "forgot AuthTip")
   - exhaustive — switch covers all enum values
   - gosec — security patterns
   - staticcheck — already standard
   - bodyclose — http response body close
   - rowserrcheck — sql rows.Err()
   - sqlclosecheck — sql resource leaks

2. Run `golangci-lint run ./...` and fix every finding from the new linters.
   Existing semgrep rules already in tools/semgrep/ remain a separate lane.

3. Add to Makefile: `make lint` runs golangci-lint AND semgrep.

4. Document in CONTRIBUTING (or README) the lint-pass requirement
   for PRs.

## Acceptance

- golangci-lint run ./... exits 0
- Full Go test suite green
- Integration suites green
- `make lint` works (or no-ops cleanly when semgrep not installed)

## Bug classes eliminated

- "silent error swallow" (15% of all bugs found)
- "half-init struct" subset of "missing check"
- Some Go-specific gotchas

## Effort

1 day. Highest ROI item — passive guardrail that doesn't require any
code restructuring, just turning on the right lints.
result:
golangci-lint configured with 9 linters tuned for the bug classes
observed in past review rounds. From 85 raw findings → 0 issues.

## What landed

- `.golangci.yml` v2 schema, 9 linters enabled
- `make lint` → vet + golangci + semgrep (all 3 lanes)
- 23 source files updated to clear findings (10 unused deletions,
  4 staticcheck fixes, 3 bodyclose, 1 sqlclosecheck, 1 ineffassign,
  5 explicit errcheck, false-positive gosec excludes documented)
- `proto/cbor.go`: IntDecConvertSigned → IntDecConvertSignedOrFail
  (preferred per cbor library deprecation)

## Verification
- `make lint` → 0 issues
- Full Go test suite green (incl. invariants 1500 random ops)
- 17 integration suites green (no behavior change)

## Bug classes now CI-blocked
- Silent error swallowing (15% of past bugs)
- HTTP body leaks
- SQL resource leaks
- Half-init structs (eventually via exhaustruct — currently disabled
  pending broader struct-init review; tracked as follow-up)
- Dead code drift

## Notes
- gosec G115 (integer overflow) excluded — too noisy for our
  uint64↔int64 CBOR/SQLite domain. Real overflow risks handled
  at validate layer.
- gosec G704 (SSRF) excluded — server URL is the SSRF target by
  design. Pinning ceremony per TRANSLOG.md §6.1 binds it.

name: Wave C: Newtype-wrapper for validated values
description:
Convert "validation strings" passed around as raw types into newtype
wrappers with private constructors. The compiler then enforces that
any value of the type was validated at construction.

Bug pattern this eliminates: "missing check" (40% of all bugs found) +
URL canonicalization drift + path traversal.

## Newtypes to introduce

### `internal/canon/url.go` — CanonicalServerURL

```go
type CanonicalURL struct{ s string }

func ParseURL(raw string) (CanonicalURL, error) {
    // lowercase scheme/host, strip trailing slash, drop frag/query
    s, err := normalize(raw)
    if err != nil { return CanonicalURL{}, err }
    return CanonicalURL{s: s}, nil
}

func (u CanonicalURL) String() string { return u.s }
```

Replaces the current `serverURL string` parameter in:
- `internal/cli/sync.go` (every helper)
- `internal/cli/witness_check.go`
- `internal/witness/store.go` (PinServer etc.)

Use `CanonicalURL` instead of raw `string` for all server URLs.

### `internal/proto/scopeid.go` — ScopeID

```go
type ScopeID struct{ s string }

func ParseScopeID(raw string) (ScopeID, error) {
    if !isValidShape(raw) { return ScopeID{}, errBadScope }
    return ScopeID{s: raw}, nil
}
```

Replaces `scopeID string` parameter. The path traversal bug
(fdhome.go:51) becomes structurally impossible — you can't pass
`../etc/passwd` into a function that takes `ScopeID`.

### `internal/crypto/keys.go` — Ed25519Pub / Ed25519Priv

```go
type Ed25519Pub [32]byte    // fixed-array, len always 32
type Ed25519Priv [64]byte   // fixed-array, len always 64

func ParseEd25519Pub(raw []byte) (Ed25519Pub, error)
```

Eliminates "wrong-key-size panic" bugs. Replaces `pub []byte` /
`priv []byte` throughout the codebase.

## Acceptance

- All callers updated (large refactor)
- All tests green
- Internal types only — no proto/wire change
- Compiler enforces: a function taking `CanonicalURL` cannot be called
  with raw `string` without explicit ParseURL

## Bug classes eliminated

- Path traversal (fdhome.go:51) → impossible
- Cross-server replay (httpsig.go) → still need server_pub binding,
  but URL drift between client/server eliminated
- ed25519.Sign/Verify panic on wrong-size key → impossible
- "Trailing slash drift between sync and witness" → impossible

## Effort

2-3 days. Many call sites to update, but each is mechanical.

## Dependencies

Should land AFTER Wave B (smaller files = easier to refactor).

name: Restore recovery bundles atomically in CLI and Desktop
description: Implement v2 import without requesting a new device passphrase. Stage and validate every file before replacing local state, refuse unintended overwrite, and roll back cleanly on failure. Import stages and fsyncs both files, commits without overwrite, rolls back partial installs, keeps the selected file on retry, and starts the managed agent only after restoration.

name: S2/S3: encrypted key import — passphrase ignored on raw extract, encrypted RSA/ECDSA stored unusable
description: sshkey.go:116 (ed25519 path) calls ssh.ParseRawPrivateKey without passphrase even when caller provided one. sshkey.go:139 (RSA/ECDSA path) stores the encrypted PEM as-is; later Signer() re-parses without passphrase and fails. Fix: use ParseRawPrivateKeyWithPassphrase when passphrase is set; for RSA/ECDSA either decrypt-then-re-encode under a known marker, OR reject encrypted non-ed25519 with a clear error.
result: S2: ImportOpenSSH ed25519 path now calls ssh.ParseRawPrivateKeyWithPassphrase when caller supplied a passphrase — previously it always called the no-passphrase variant and silently hit the 'unable to extract raw key' fallback. S3: RSA + ECDSA paths now refuse encrypted PEMs with a clear error directing the user to ssh-keygen -p -N '' (or to rotate to ed25519 which fd0 supports natively). Encryption is detected via passphrase-presence OR PEM 'ENCRYPTED' marker. Avoids storing a blob that Signer() would later be unable to decrypt. Tests pass.

name: Analyze fd0 projection refresh UX gaps

name: Plan browser and OS password autofill
description: Define a KISS architecture and staged delivery plan for fd0 password autofill on macOS and Linux, with Chrome and Firefox support. Base the plan on the existing URL lookup, Desktop bridge, agent and release pipeline. Separate the cross-platform WebExtension/native-messaging path from Apple's native AutoFill Credential Provider extension. Identify security boundaries, URL matching hardening, packaging/signing constraints, browser compatibility, test matrix, and explicit non-goals. Planning only; no product code changes.

Build one TypeScript Manifest V3 WebExtension for Chrome and Firefox, backed by a narrow Go native-messaging host that reuses fd0 domain logic but never exposes the general Desktop bridge. Harden URL matching with canonical origins and public-suffix rejection; keep secrets out of extension storage and require user-triggered fill. Ship password/username first, then TOTP and save/update. Treat native macOS AutoFill as a separate Swift AuthenticationServices credential-provider target after an entitlement, signing and secure App Group/XPC data-access spike. Linux has no equivalent standard autofill provider; Chrome/Firefox are the supported Linux integration. Include installer registration, release signing, website/skill docs and isolated browser/OS tests. No product code changed.

name: Ship polished browser autofill
description: Build fd0 browser integration for Chrome/Chromium and Firefox on macOS and Linux as a release-quality login lifecycle, not a thin password fill demo. Scope: username/password autofill, multiple-match selection, strong password suggestions and full generator, create/update login flows, TOTP QR/paste onboarding, and seamless TOTP fill after a user-selected login. Architecture: one shared TypeScript Manifest V3 WebExtension plus a narrow Go native-messaging host that talks directly to fd0 domain APIs. The extension must never persist credentials; content-script messages are untrusted; native requests are origin-bound; item updates are identity- and revision-bound. UI must match fd0 Desktop, isolate itself from page CSS, support keyboard/screen readers/light/dark/reduced motion, and fail calmly when fd0 is locked or unavailable. Acceptance: isolated Go and browser tests, hostile/edge-case form fixture corpus, Chromium and Firefox smoke coverage, installer registration for supported desktop packages, signed-package-ready artifacts, website and fd0 skill documentation, and no access to real ~/.fd0 during tests.

Standalone CLI update behavior must remain unchanged. Desktop-only flags that cannot be honored must fail clearly rather than silently changing semantics. Acceptance: relevant shell, Go, renderer, Electron, and updater tests pass; packaged behavior remains signed and agent-safe; no second implementation downloads or replaces the Desktop bundle.

Updated Desktop, website, and fd0 skill documentation. All scoped and broad verification passed; changes remain uncommitted on feat/desktop-install-update-polish for review.

name: Decompose sealed-box: parseSealed + Card interface + MockCard
description:
Goal: split the on-card sealed-box open into a hardware-only step (ECDH) and pure-software steps (parse, key derive, AEAD open). After this task the only hardware-dependent function is Card.SharedSecret.

Steps:
1. internal/crypto/sealedbox.go (new): add ParseSealed(sealed) → (ephPub [32]byte, ct []byte). Validates len(sealed) ≥ 32 + 16 (eph + Poly1305 tag minimum); rejects on short input.

2. internal/crypto/yubikey/yubikey.go: add interface
     type Card interface {
         SharedSecret(ephPub []byte) ([]byte, error) // 32-byte X25519 ECDH output
         PublicX25519() ([]byte, error)
         Close() error
     }
   Replace existing PivKey type with Card; rename for clarity. OpenSealedBox stays on Card temporarily to preserve existing surface.

3. internal/crypto/yubikey/mockcard.go (new, !yubikey build tag OK — software-only): MockCard struct holds an X25519 priv, implements Card.SharedSecret via curve25519.X25519. Constructor NewMockCard(priv []byte) for tests.

4. Unit tests in internal/crypto/yubikey/mockcard_test.go: roundtrip — random eph pair, expect SharedSecret(ephPub) == curve25519.X25519(cardPriv, ephPub). Property-test 100 iterations.

Done when:
- ParseSealed exists with input-validation tests.
- Card interface defined.
- MockCard compiles and passes roundtrip tests.
- go build ./... and go build -tags=yubikey ./... both green.
- No behaviour change to existing call sites (OpenSealedBox still returns 'pending hardware-day integration' on real card; MockCard works).

Codex review at the end.
result: Decomposition complete. ParseSealed (sealedbox.go), Card interface (yubikey.go) replacing PivKey, MockCard (mockcard.go) implementing Card via curve25519.X25519, pivWrapper updated to satisfy Card with slot+PIN state stored at Open time. Tests: 13 new test funcs covering boundary, alias, capacity-clamp, ECDH symmetry (200 iters), RFC 7748 low-order vectors, constructor copy semantics. go test ./... green; both build configs clean. Codex review: 2 rounds, all P1/P2 resolved.

name: C4+C5: witness chain-level probes (T35 + T41)
description:
Two witness-level mitigations from the threat model:

- T41 freshness probe: GET /v1/witness/highest/{server}/{chain} returns max(tree_size) the witness has archived for that chain. Client CrossCheckSTH refuses if server_supplied < witness max.
- T35 equivocation probe: GET /v1/witness/equivocation/{server}/{chain} returns true iff witness has ever seen multi-roots at any tree_size for that chain. Client refuses any cosign on equivocated chains.

Same infrastructure (witness HTTP + client check), same testing surface — likely one commit. Update THREATS.md T35/T41 to drop the 'Wave H' todos.
result: C4 (T41 freshness probe) + C5 (T35 chain-level equivocation probe) implementiert in 4 commits + 4 codex review-runden. Witness HTTP API erweitert: GET /v1/witness/highest, GET /v1/witness/equivocation. Client CrossCheckSTH ruft probes UNCONDITIONALLY für jeden witness vor matching++, an allen 5 control-flow paths (success, not-observed, unreachable, bad-cosign, size-drift). Codex final: 'All five non-hard-refuse per-witness paths now call checkChainProbes.' THREATS.md T35/T41 'Wave H todo' jetzt geschlossen.

name: Evaluate Deno Desktop against Electron
description:
Part of fd0 desktop GUI. Before committing to Electron, validate whether the experimental Deno 2.9 Desktop surface is mature enough for fd0.

Build the same narrow vertical slice with Deno Desktop and Electron:
- SolidJS renderer with locked/status and read-only pass list/detail.
- Start the bundled Go desktop bridge and complete a version handshake over stdio.
- Package a macOS arm64 application and one Linux artifact.
- Measure clean artifact size, cold start, idle memory, and bridge latency.
- Verify renderer/backend isolation, navigation controls, binding allow-list behavior, and handling of malformed calls.
- Verify signing/notarization hooks and whether an update can atomically replace Deno code, bundled fd0, and bundled fd0-agent.
- Confirm automated end-to-end testing can drive both the native WebView and packaged app.
- Record platform differences for WKWebView and WebKitGTK.

Decision criteria:
Choose Deno Desktop only if bundled sidecars update atomically, security boundaries are testable, packaging/signing are reproducible, and required APIs are stable enough to pin. Otherwise use Electron. Deno's smaller native-WebView bundle alone is not sufficient.

Current evidence:
Deno Desktop debuted experimentally in Deno 2.9. It has native WebView or CEF backends, in-process bindings, cross-platform installer generation, and signed Ed25519 delta-update manifests. Known concerns include experimental APIs, no built-in type bridge, broad baked-in desktop permissions, platform WebView variance, manual notarization, externally managed Windows signing, and Windows auto-update not applying staged patches yet.

Done when:
A short ADR records measured results, reproduced limitations, the chosen shell, and why. No production GUI work starts before this decision.
result: Electron selected for the first fd0 desktop implementation. SolidJS and TypeScript remain the renderer stack; the Go bridge and existing fd0-agent remain the backend boundary. Deno Desktop is not on the critical path and can be reevaluated later without blocking the runnable local version.

name: Harden SFTP paths, transfers, and failure handling
description:
Perform the focused security and reliability pass required before exposing remote filesystem mutations in CLI and Desktop.

Required behavior:
- Define lexical remote-path handling without shell expansion and preserve legitimate spaces, Unicode, and leading dashes.
- Never recursively follow symlinked directories. Surface link metadata and require an explicit operation on the link itself.
- Bound tree depth, entry counts, metadata sizes, protocol frames, queued transfers, and progress frequency to prevent memory or UI exhaustion.
- Downloads write to a private temporary sibling and atomically replace only after success when the platform permits it. Uploads use a remote temporary sibling and rename where the server supports safe semantics.
- Failed and cancelled transfers clean only artifacts created by that operation and never remove an existing destination.
- Unknown host keys are never accepted automatically. GUI failures explain that the host must first be verified in Terminal.
- GUI file sessions require non-interactive key or agent authentication. Interactive CLI SFTP may retain native OpenSSH prompts.
- Redact local absolute paths, usernames, file content, SSH diagnostics, and helper protocol payloads from production logs and support snapshots.
- Map disconnected, locked, permission denied, missing SFTP subsystem, disk full, overwrite conflict, and cancellation into calm actionable product errors.

Verification:
- Add adversarial tests for traversal-like names, symlinks, deep trees, huge metadata, partial writes, disconnects, cancellation races, overwrite conflicts, malicious helper messages, and concurrent window close.
- Verify direct and ProxyJump argv behavior without connecting to real infrastructure.
- Run the repository security and release policy checks relevant to new dependencies and packaged subprocesses.
result: Hardened SFTP with strict host checking and BatchMode GUI sessions, direct argv execution, NUL/path/frame/entry/depth bounds, bounded concurrent operations and Desktop transfers, progress throttling, private atomic temp destinations, exact-byte copying, cancellation cleanup, recursive symlink refusal, explicit overwrite/delete controls, redacted public errors, reconnect behavior, and adversarial tests for Unicode/spaces/leading dashes, symlinks, cancellation, oversized metadata, disk-full/disconnect/auth failures, and packaged subprocess presence.

name: Move desktop agent lifecycle to native per-user supervision
description:
Severity: P1 release blocker.

Problem:
fd0-agent is currently started with exec.Command and managed through PID/socket files. There is no launchd or systemd restart policy. The desktop Open at login toggle uses Electron setLoginItemSettings with deprecated openAsHidden behavior, is unsupported on Linux, and conflates starting the GUI with running the background agent. Explicit application quit does not lock the agent immediately. An already-unlocked agent is accepted before desktop bundle version/flavor compatibility is enforced.

Required approach:
- Make the bundled fd0-agent a native per-user service that always starts locked.
- macOS 13+: bundle and register a LaunchAgent through SMAppService, with visible approval/status handling.
- Linux: install and manage a systemd --user service with Restart=on-failure; do not require lingering beyond logout.
- Separate settings for background service availability and opening the full GUI at login.
- Define one owner for install, start, stop, restart, update, and uninstall so native service management and legacy manual spawn cannot race.
- On explicit Quit, apply a documented security policy; for the consumer app, lock immediately unless the user explicitly chose background-unlocked behavior.
- Before any privileged operation, resolve or block agent version/flavor mismatch, including manual DMG replacement and unknown legacy metadata.
- Repair stale sockets and PID files through the supervisor without touching unrelated fd0 homes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Agent crash, stale socket, login, logout, suspend/resume, GUI restart, explicit Quit, bundle update, and uninstall behave deterministically on macOS and Linux.
- The GUI can start when the service is stopped and repair it without a terminal.
- The service never starts unlocked and secrets remain inaccessible after the configured lock boundary.
- Existing user vaults, sockets, SSH integration, CLI use, and isolated dev homes remain safe.
- Platform-native integration and clean-machine tests cover both architectures.
result: Added one native lifecycle owner for fd0-agent: SMAppService LaunchAgent on macOS 13+ and systemd --user with restart-on-failure on Linux. GUI login is separate, explicit Quit locks, updater/uninstall/CLI stop and restart delegate to the supervisor, incompatible or metadata-less agents are replaced before unlock, and custom FD0_HOME/FD0_SSH_SOCK remain on the isolated legacy path. Verified packaged LaunchAgent structure and ad-hoc signature, Desktop E2E, 26 unit tests, Go tests, and 13 isolated lifecycle scenarios.

name: Doc language pass: KISS/DRY rewrite
description:
Goal: rewrite all .md docs in plain English, terse and clear, no filler.

Principles (caveman-skill inspired, but normal English):
- Clear, neutral, short. No verbose filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply).
- KISS: prefer simple sentences over compound.
- DRY: no major content duplication across or within docs.
- Bullet hygiene: each bullet a distinct topic. No theme spread across multiple bullets. No theme repetition.
- Technical accuracy: 100%. Verify against code.

Files (in order):
1. README.md
2. PROTOCOL.md
3. API.md
4. STORAGE.md
5. TRANSLOG.md
6. THREATS.md (careful — threat IDs and code refs must stay correct)
7. BENCH.md
8. TODO.md
9. tools/semgrep/README.md
10. internal/wirecompat/testdata/v1/README.md

Each file: rewrite, then codex review, iterate until clean. No content drops, no factual changes — only language.

name: Build the OpenSSH-backed SFTP transport
description:
Implement the shared Go transport beneath CLI and Desktop file operations.

Approach:
- Add a focused SFTP protocol dependency and keep native OpenSSH in charge of connection setup.
- Reuse the existing fd0 host lookup and regenerated composite SSH configuration.
- Spawn the resolved ssh executable with an argv equivalent to ssh -F <config> <alias> -s sftp; never invoke a shell.
- Preserve fd0-agent IdentityAgent behavior, ProxyJump, user SSH options, and Known Hosts verification.
- Provide typed list, stat, open/read, create/write, mkdir, rename, and remove operations plus explicit session close and context cancellation.
- Convert authentication, unknown-host, missing-subsystem, permission, disconnect, and not-found failures into stable domain errors.

Reliability and safety:
- Do not auto-accept host keys or weaken StrictHostKeyChecking.
- Treat paths as protocol data, not commands.
- Bound metadata and recursive traversal; do not follow directory symlinks recursively.
- Ensure child processes and partial handles close on cancellation or parent exit.
- Never log file contents, private local paths, or secrets.

Verification:
- Unit-test argv construction, validation, error mapping, cancellation, and process cleanup.
- Use isolated temporary FD0 and SSH paths plus a deterministic fake SSH/SFTP subsystem; never touch the real user vault, agent socket, SSH config, or remote hosts.
- Prove exact-byte reads and writes including spaces, Unicode, leading dashes, and control-character rejection where display safety requires it.
result: Implemented shared OpenSSH-backed SFTP transport using the exact fd0-rendered SSH configuration, strict host verification, direct argv spawning, exact-byte and recursive transfers, atomic temporary destinations, private local modes, symlink-safe deletion, bounded stderr, cancellation, and isolated transport tests. Verified with go test ./internal/sftpclient.

name: Wave G: Threat-model annotations (optional)
description:
Optional / lowest priority. Codify "what threat does this code defend
against" as code annotations.

## Pattern

```go
// THREAT: cross-server replay
// MITIGATION: server_pub bound in HTTPSignedInput per TRANSLOG.md §x
// AUDIT: codex security audit 2026-05
func verifyHTTPSig(...) { ... }
```

Linter rule: any function in `server/auth.go`, `cli/witness_check.go`,
`agent/server.go` (security-critical paths) MUST have a `// THREAT:`
annotation. Removes "I forgot why this check is here, can I delete it?"
class of regression.

## Acceptance

- Every security-critical function annotated.
- Custom semgrep rule fires on any new function in those files
  without a THREAT annotation.

## Effort

1-2 days. Mostly writing comments + one new semgrep rule.

## Status

Lowest priority. Nice-to-have. Reserve for post-v1.0.

name: Harden desktop dependency and release supply chain
description:
Severity: P1 release blocker.

Problem:
bun audit reports high-severity GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx through fast-uri 3.1.3 in the electron-builder build dependency chain; patched 3.x is 3.1.4. Electron is one patch behind the current release. The desktop workflow pins actions by commit, but the CLI release workflow still uses mutable action tags and goreleaser version latest. A desktop release therefore cannot yet claim a clean, reproducible supply chain.

Required approach:
- Upgrade or override fast-uri to a patched version and prove bun audit is clean; do not suppress the advisory without exploitability evidence.
- Update Electron to the current supported patch after unit, E2E, packaging, and security-regression verification.
- Pin all release workflow actions by immutable commit SHA and pin an exact GoReleaser version.
- Keep Bun, Go, electron-builder, electron-updater, and release tooling reproducible through frozen lockfiles and explicit versions.
- Add dependency and artifact SBOM/provenance checks appropriate for public desktop artifacts.
- Treat build-time vulnerabilities as release blockers even when they are not shipped in the renderer.

Acceptance criteria:
- bun audit has no unresolved high or critical advisories.
- Release jobs are reproducible from a clean checkout with immutable tool versions.
- Signed artifacts identify the exact source commit, dependency lock, architecture, and workflow identity.
- Electron security configuration remains intact after dependency updates.
- Automated policy prevents mutable release tooling or known high/critical dependencies from entering a release tag.
result: Hardened the dependency and release supply chain. Upgraded Electron, forced patched fast-uri/brace-expansion/postcss/tar versions, made bun audit clean, pinned every release action and GoReleaser version, enforced the policy on normal CI and release tags, and added SPDX SBOM plus GitHub provenance. The draft release is published only after all artifacts, authenticated manifest, embedded-verifier validation, and attestations exist. Frozen install, audit, Actionlint, policy, package build, Go verification, and desktop E2E pass.

name: Apply defense-in-depth review follow-ups
description: Address the six suppressed security-review candidates where low-cost hardening improves resilience without treating them as validated vulnerabilities. Cover terminal control neutralization for remote labels, explicit secret wiping on rejected unlock paths where ownership is clear, archive extraction containment as a defense-in-depth invariant, and fail-closed cleanup/error handling where it can be improved without data loss. Reassess each suppressed candidate; document when no code change is justified. Acceptance: focused regression tests, no v1 format break, no user-data deletion, and an evidence-backed disposition for all six suppressed candidates.
result: All six suppressed candidates received low-risk hardening: exact-member streamed shell extraction with traversal fixture (CAN-009), terminal control neutralization for shared labels and witness status (CAN-013/049), fail-closed startup peer revocation (CAN-032), no pre-verification execution of target binaries (CAN-035), and centralized clearing of decrypted rejected-unlock material (CAN-040). Focused Go, race, shell syntax, and isolated installer E2E tests passed; production fd0 PID/socket/binaries remained unchanged.

name: fd0 structural refactor: eliminate bug classes via type-driven design
description:
Master epic for the fd0.sh structural refactor that eliminates the bug
classes uncovered across multiple review rounds.

## Background

After 8 commits of bug-fixes (Hardening Wave 1-3 + 3 review-round waves
+ test diversification), bug analysis shows:

- **~50 critical bugs** total found across all review rounds
- **30% concentrated in cli/sync.go** (1 file = bug magnet)
- **60% are "missing check" + "wrong ordering"** — type-system failures
- **15% silent error swallowing** — trivial linter catches
- **10% Go-specific gotchas** — slice cap leak, KeepAlive elision, decoder aliasing
- **10% spec drift** — implementation doesn't match PROTOCOL.md

## Goal

Reduce residual bug rate to ~30% of current via structural changes that
make the dominant bug classes COMPILE-TIME or LINT-TIME impossible,
not just test-time detectable.

## Wave plan (in order of ROI/effort)

- Wave A: Linter hygiene (1 day) — errcheck, exhaustruct, semgrep CI gate.
- Wave B: Decompose cli/sync.go (1 day) — split 1500-LOC god-object into 5 files.
- Wave C: Newtype-wrappers (2-3 days) — CanonicalURL, ScopeID, Ed25519Pub.
- Wave D: VerifiedSTH type-state (1 day) — verify-before-commit at type level.
- Wave E: chain.Tx transactional file ops (3 days) — replace manual rollback.
- Wave F: Spec compliance generator (optional) — parse PROTOCOL.md MUSTs into tests.
- Wave G: Threat-model annotations (optional) — // THREAT: comments on security boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- All Go tests + 17 integration suites green at every wave commit boundary.
- Each wave is its own commit with the bug class it eliminates.
- After A+B: bug density per LOC measurably lower in sync.go.
- After C+D: spec drift + cross-server replay class structurally impossible.
- After E: silent truncate-rollback failures structurally impossible.

## Status

User approved A+B execution now. C-G remain as queued tasks for follow-up
sessions.

name: T6: role-add accepts non-admin source as issuer; fails at talosctl with opaque error
description: talos_native.go RunTalosRoleAdd takes any --from context and writes it as a temp talosconfig for 'talosctl config new'. If the source has os:reader role (or anything below os:admin), talosctl returns a permissions error that fd0 wraps with 'talosctl config new: …'. Fix: in talos_native.go, after lookupTalosContext, verify src.Role is RoleAdmin (or empty — unknown roles fall through to talosctl). Print a clear 'role-add requires an admin issuer; %q has role %q' error.
result: RunTalosRoleAdd now rejects known non-admin source roles (os:reader, os:etcd:backup, os:impersonator) with a clear 'minting new certs requires os:admin' error. Unknown/empty roles still fall through to talosctl so Talos additions stay forward-compatible.
